signals.title: [Bug]: hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort emits a false unrecognized-key warning
signals.text: ### Bug Description `agent.reasoning_effort` is a documented and runtime-consumed configuration key, but setting it through `hermes config set` emits an unrecognized-key warning. The value is still saved to `config.yaml` and returned by `hermes config get`, so the problem is the false warning rather than persistence or runtime behavior. This report concerns the scalar global key `agent.reasoning_effort`, not the per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides` mapping. The documentation only excludes nested `reasoning_overrides` entries from `hermes config set` because model names may contain dots. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run: ```shell hermes config set agent.reasoning_effort high ``` 2. Observe the warning. 3. Confirm that the value was saved: ```shell hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort ``` ### Expected Behavior Because `agent.reasoning_effort` is a documented and runtime-supported key, it should be saved without an unrecognized-key warning. If `/reasoning high --global` is intentionally the only supported setter, the CLI should direct users to that command instead of saying Hermes may not read the saved value. ### Actual Behavior The value is saved, ```text ✓ Set agent.reasoning_effort = high in <config path> ``` but the CLI prints: ```text ⚠ 'agent.reasoning_effort' is not a recognized config key — it was saved anyway, but Hermes may not read it. Did you mean: agent.reasoning_overrides ``` `hermes config get agent.reasoning_effort` subsequently returns: ```text high ``` ### Affected Component CLI (interactive chat), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell hermes debug share output can be attached if needed. ``` ### Operating System Debian 13 ### Python Version 3.13.5 ### Hermes Version 0.20.0 ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) _No response_ ### Proposed Fix (optional) _No response_ ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

signals.title: [Bug]: hermes update stalls at autostash restore prompt on macOS — post-update gateway restart never runs, gateway serves stale code
signals.text: ## Summary On macOS, `hermes update` can stall at the autostash-restore interactive prompt ("Restore local changes now? [Y/n]"). When that happens the process never reaches the post-update gateway-restart block, so a launchd-supervised gateway keeps running with pre-update modules in memory while lazily importing post-update code from disk — a mixed/stale runtime that fails later with confusing errors. ## Environment - macOS (launchd-managed gateway, `ai.hermes.gateway`) - Direct upstream checkout (NOT a fork — the #73108 fork case is a different trigger) - Hermes v0.20.0 (2026.8.3), updated 2026-08-13 to `fa83af3f9` ## Observed timeline (from ~/.hermes/logs/update.log and gateway-exit-diag.log) 1. `2026-08-13T22:25:06` — `hermes update` starts. Local changes detected → autostash created (`hermes-update-autostash-20260813-142640`). Found 4231 new commits, pulled them. 2. Update prints the restore prompt and **stalls there**. `update.log` ends at `Restore local changes now? [Y/n]` — no further output. The stash entry is still present afterwards (`git stash list` shows `stash@{0}: On main: hermes-update-autostash-20260813-142640`), i.e. the update never completed its restore step, hence never reached the restart block. 3. The gateway process (PID 20465, started 2026-08-13 21:45) kept running on the pre-update code for ~12 hours. 4. `2026-08-14 01:40:22 UTC` — gateway exits non-zero (`gateway.exit_nonzero` in gateway-exit-diag.log), 30s later a manual `launchctl kickstart -k` brings it back on the new code. Only then does the mixed-runtime error go away. The same autostash pattern also appears at 07-25 and 05-20 (older `hermes-update-autostash-*` entries), suggesting the prompt regularly stalls when the update runs in a context where stdin is not attended (e.g. run from an IDE/terminal that closed, or a non-interactive wrapper). ## Root cause In `hermes_cli/update_cmd.py`, `_restore_stashed_changes()` blocks on `input()` (or `_gateway_prompt`) before the gateway-restart block in `_cmd_update_impl()` runs. If the prompt never gets a response (closed stdin, unattended terminal, EOF handling paths), the update either hangs or takes the skip-restore path and the **gateway fleet restart is skipped entirely** — there is no timeout on the prompt and no "restart gateways even though restore was skipped" guarantee. The post-update restart logic exists (launchd/systemd/manual-PID branches, added around 84a875ca0 / 988ecc742) but it is downstream of an interactive prompt that can block indefinitely. Related: #73108 is the same symptom family (post-update restart skipped) but triggered by the fork "Already up to date" early-exit; its fix PR #73679 is still open. This report is the direct-upstream counterpart: the restart is skipped whenever the update path is interrupted before the restart block, and the autostash prompt is one such interruption point. ## Expected behavior - The post-update gateway restart should run even when stash restore is skipped or times out (restart is independent of restore). - The autostash prompt should have a timeout / non-interactive default so an unattended `hermes update` does not hang mid-update with a gateway left on stale code. - At minimum, when a running gateway could not be restarted, print explicit guidance (the managed-runtime repair path already does this with "Restart required to finish..." — plain source-tree updates emit neither a warning nor a restart). ## Workaround Manually restart the launchd service after every `hermes update` (e.g. kickstart the `ai.hermes.gateway` label), or chain the restart onto the update command.
signals.author: Feahter

signals.title: session_search discovery hides ALL hits from the current session's own /new-reset lineage (gateway recall goes blind)
signals.text: ## Summary In gateway conversations (QQ/Telegram/etc.), every `/new` creates a child session via `parent_session_id`. `session_search` discovery excludes any hit whose lineage root equals the *current* session's lineage root (`tools/session_search_tool.py`, the `current_lineage_root == lineage_root` guard), on the assumption that same-lineage content is already in the active context. That assumption holds for compression continuations but is false for manual `/new` resets, which carry no transcript. Result: after each `/new`, the agent cannot recall *any* previous session of the same chat — `session_search` returns 0 results even though messages, FTS, and vector indexes are all intact. ## Reproduction (real state.db) Chain: `20260812_152906` → child `20260813_083223` → child `20260814_083525` (current). - `session_search(query="布洛芬")` from the current session → **0 results** - Direct SQL on the same DB: `messages_fts_trigram MATCH '布洛芬'` → 12 rows, all joined correctly to `20260813_083223` - Browse mode (`session_search()` with no args) shows only cron sessions, because every recent interactive session has a `parent_session_id` and is skipped Concrete user impact: the user asked the agent "do you remember what we talked about last night?" — the agent searched, got 0 results, and wrongly concluded no conversation had happened, when in fact a full 167-message session existed. ## Root cause - Discovery guard: `tools/session_search_tool.py` (~L641) `if current_lineage_root and lineage_root == current_lineage_root: continue` - Browse skip: (~L451) `if s.get("parent_session_id"): continue` - `_resolve_lineage()` already computes `has_compression_hop` to distinguish compression splits from other children, but both guards ignore it and treat all lineage children as in-context. ## Expected behavior The current-lineage exclusion should apply only when the lineage hop is a compression continuation (content actually carried forward). `/new`-reset children should be discoverable and browsable like any other session. ## Related, not duplicate - #82988 — browse drops resumed conversations (the list-side symptom) - #6507 — child hit summarized at the lineage root (the transcript-side symptom) - This one is the *current-lineage exclusion* — a third defect in the same neighborhood.
signals.author: Lavinia-ai

signals.title: [Bug]: PermissionError in _find_git_root() crashes system prompt building for gateway-mode agents
signals.text: ### Bug Description When an agent runs via hermes gateway run -p <profile>, the gateway bridges config.yaml’s terminal.cwd into the TERMINAL_CWD environment variable. During system prompt construction, build_context_files_prompt() calls resolve_context_cwd() which reads TERMINAL_CWD, then passes it to _find_git_root(Path(cwd)). If terminal.cwd points to a directory the agent process user cannot access (e.g., /root on a server where the agent runs as a non-root user like kduser), _find_git_root() crashes with: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.git' This causes the entire system prompt build to fail, and the agent responds with “Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error” on every message. ### Steps to Reproduce Set terminal.cwd: /root in a profile’s config.yaml (this is the Docker sandbox default on many setups) Ensure the gateway process runs as a non-root user (e.g., kduser) that cannot access /root Start the agent via hermes gateway run -p <profile> Send a message to the agent (via webhook, yunzhijia, or any messaging platform) Agent responds with “Sorry, I encountered an unexpected error” — check agent.log for PermissionError ### Expected Behavior _find_git_root() should gracefully handle PermissionError by treating inaccessible directories as “no .git found” and continuing the search (or returning None). The system prompt should build successfully regardless of whether the cwd is accessible. ### Actual Behavior Traceback (most recent call last): File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/system_prompt.py", line 473, in build_system_prompt_parts context_files_prompt = _r.build_context_files_prompt( File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 2074, in build_context_files_prompt _load_hermes_md(cwd_path, context_length) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 1921, in _load_hermes_md hermes_md_path = _find_hermes_md(cwd_path) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 100, in _find_hermes_md stop_at = _find_git_root(cwd) File "/var/lib/hermes-agent/agent/prompt_builder.py", line 85, in _find_git_root if (parent / ".git").exists(): File "/usr/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1236, in exists self.stat() File "/usr/lib/python3.11/pathlib.py", line 1014, in stat return os.stat(self, follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks) PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/root/.git' ### Affected Component Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp) ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) N/A (CLI only) ### Debug Report ```shell <!-- Run hermes debug share and paste links here --> ``` ### Operating System Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (5.15.0-179-generic) ### Python Version Python 3.11.x ### Hermes Version v0.19.0 (git: v2026.7.20-995-ga61183b56f) ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell See Actual Behavior above for full traceback. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) agent/prompt_builder.py, line 85, in _find_git_root(): def _find_git_root(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]: current = start.resolve() for parent in [current, *current.parents]: if (parent / ".git").exists(): # ← .exists() raises PermissionError on inaccessible dirs return parent return None Path.exists() calls os.stat(), which raises PermissionError when the directory itself is not accessible — not just when .git doesn’t exist. The function has no try/except PermissionError. Why it only affects gateway mode: gateway/run.py bridges config.yaml’s terminal.cwd into os.environ["TERMINAL_CWD"] (line ~2072-2087). resolve_context_cwd() in system_prompt.py reads TERMINAL_CWD and passes it to build_context_files_prompt(cwd=...). In CLI/Web UI mode, TERMINAL_CWD is not set, so resolve_context_cwd() returns None and build_context_files_prompt falls back to os.getcwd() — which is typically the user’s accessible home directory. Why /root: Docker sandbox deployments commonly set terminal.cwd: /root (the container’s default home). This works inside the container (overlay filesystem), but the gateway process runs on the host as a non-root user who cannot access /root. Verified: upstream origin/main also unfixed — same code without try/except PermissionError. ### Proposed Fix (optional) def _find_git_root(start: Path) -> Optional[Path]: current = start.resolve() for parent in [current, *current.parents]: try: if (parent / ".git").exists(): return parent except PermissionError: continue return None One-line try/except PermissionError — skip inaccessible directories, return None if no .git found. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR
signals.author: shamolvshu

signals.title: [Feature]: Bridge $currentProvider into host.state so plugins can show the live provider
signals.text: ## Summary The plugin SDK bridges the live model (`host.state.model`) but not the live provider, even though the app store holds it (`$currentProvider`). A status-bar plugin that shows `provider · model` at a glance (to catch misconfigured provider kicks) therefore displays the *configured* provider, not the one actually selected for the session. ## Repro 1. Install a status-bar plugin reading `host.state.model` + `config.get {key:'full'}` → `config.model.provider` (the standard recipe). 2. Open the model picker and select provider `nous`, model `longcat`. 3. The pill updates to `… · longcat` (model is bridged) but the provider segment still shows the configured default (`opencode-go`). Expected: the pill shows `nous · longcat` — the pair the user actually selected. ## Why The picker writes **two separate atoms** (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-model-controls.ts:183-184`): ```ts setCurrentModel(selection.model) setCurrentProvider(selection.provider) ``` but `host.state` bridges only one of them (`apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts:59-73`): ```ts state: { activeSessionId: readonlyAtom<null | string>($activeSessionId), cwd: readonlyAtom<string>($currentCwd), gateway: readonlyAtom<string>($gatewayState), /** Current main model slug. */ model: readonlyAtom<string>($currentModel), profile: readonlyAtom<string>($activeGatewayProfile), viewport: readonlyAtom<ViewportRect>($viewport) } ``` The provider atom exists and is persisted (`apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts:569`): ```ts export const $currentProvider = atom(storedString(COMPOSER_PROVIDER_KEY) ?? '') ``` Plugins have no RPC door to it either (the `/api/model/info` bridge endpoint is desktop-bridge-only, not reachable from a plugin). ## Proposed fix Mirror the `model` atom — add to `host.state`: ```ts /** Current main provider slug. */ provider: readonlyAtom<string>($currentProvider), ``` The import for `$currentProvider` is already in the SDK module's dependency chain (same store file as `$currentModel`). ~3 lines, no behavioral change for existing plugins (additive surface). ## Notes - The composer's own UI reads the same `$currentProvider` atom (`model-picker-overlay.tsx:26`), so the value bridged would be exactly what the picker shows. - Per-session overrides (tile/session-scoped picks) write the same atoms via `sessionTileDelegate().updateSession(…)` confirm path — the bridge would reflect the primary session the way `model` already does.
signals.author: exergonic

signals.title: fix(desktop): local profile switch reuses default socket after update
signals.text: ## Summary After a recent Desktop update, selecting any local named profile from the profile rail can leave Desktop attached to the default profile. The named backend starts successfully, but Desktop never opens its persistent WebSocket and continues using the primary/default socket. This affects current `main` and makes local multi-profile switching appear inert: the profile is selectable, but the sidebar/active agent remains on the same profile. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop on macOS 26.6.1 (Apple silicon) - Local primary profile: `default` - Local named profile: `fiction-writer` - Reproduced from current `main` around `486f4ace20ba75401681c0915ab79a0968fa6bb1` - Confirmed still present after fetching current `origin/main` ## Reproduction 1. Configure Desktop with the local `default` profile and at least one local named profile. 2. Launch Desktop on `default`. 3. Select the named profile from the profile rail. 4. Observe that the named backend starts and passes the one-shot WebSocket probe. 5. Observe that no persistent WebSocket is opened for the named profile and the Desktop context remains attached to the primary/default socket. ## Expected behavior A local named profile should use its own pooled backend and persistent WebSocket. The sidebar, sessions, model, tools, and agent context should move to that profile. ## Actual behavior The local pooled descriptor is mistaken for a shared-primary descriptor. Desktop reuses the primary/default socket instead of dialing the named profile's pooled backend. Representative log sequence: ```text Starting Hermes backend for profile "fiction-writer" ... HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=64271 Hermes backend listening on 127.0.0.1:64271 ... tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted ... tui_gateway.ws: ws closed ... messages=0 ``` The accepted/closed connection is the startup probe. There is no subsequent persistent profile WebSocket. ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts::sharedPrimaryRoute()` currently treats the presence of `connection.profile` as proof that the descriptor uses the shared primary backend: ```ts return Boolean(conn && typeof conn === 'object' && (conn as { profile?: string }).profile) ``` However, `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts::spawnPoolBackend()` intentionally returns `profile` for local pooled descriptors as well. That profile value is needed so fresh WebSocket URL minting targets the correct backend. Therefore both of these descriptors carry `profile`: - a profile scoped onto the shared primary backend; - a dedicated local/remote pooled backend. The discriminator conflates those two routes. `ensureGatewayForProfile()` then takes the shared-primary branch for a local pool profile and never dials its socket. ## Proposed fix Add an explicit `sharedPrimary` marker only when `ensureBackend()` returns a profile-scoped primary descriptor, and make `sharedPrimaryRoute()` check that marker rather than inferring route ownership from `profile`. A regression test should assert both sides of the invariant: - `{ profile, sharedPrimary: true }` activates the primary socket; - a pooled descriptor carrying `{ profile }` still dials its own socket. ## Verification The proposed patch was tested locally: ```text Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 13 passed (13) ``` Commands: ```bash cd apps/desktop npm test -- --run src/store/gateway-shared-remote.test.ts src/store/profile.test.ts npm run typecheck npm run pack ``` After installing the rebuilt package and restarting Desktop, switching between `default` and the local named profile works normally again.
signals.author: wdon

signals.title: [Bug]: grok-4.6 reasoning effort silently dropped; max/ultra 400 on send path
signals.text: ## Bug Description When using an xAI OAuth account (grok-4.6 / grok-4.5), the reasoning-effort setting is either **silently ignored** or **hard-fails the request with HTTP 400**, depending on the level chosen. Two distinct defects on the send path (not the picker): **A. `grok-4.6` is missing from the `grok_supports_reasoning_effort` allowlist** (`agent/model_metadata.py`, ~line 555). Any effort selected for grok-4.6 is never attached to the request at all — the UI shows a choice that has zero effect. Verified live against `api.x.ai` (`/v1/responses`): grok-4.6 **accepts** `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`. **B. Unsupported levels (`max`, `ultra`) are sent verbatim and fail the whole request** with `400 Invalid reasoning effort`. There is no per-model clamp on the send path — only a hard-coded xAI map in `agent/transports/codex.py` that predates 4.6 (it folds `xhigh`→`high`, which is wrong for 4.6) and is not driven by model metadata. Also: grok-4.6 **cannot disable thinking** (`reasoning: {effort: none}` / `thinking.disabled` unsupported), yet the picker offers an Off toggle. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure Hermes with an xAI OAuth account, select `grok-4.6`. 2. Set reasoning effort to `high` in the desktop model menu. 3. Inspect the outgoing request body: no `reasoning.effort` field at all (allowlist miss → silently dropped). Expected: `reasoning: {effort: "high"}`. 4. Set effort to `max` or `ultra` (e.g. a pre-existing saved value): request fails with `400 {"error": "Invalid reasoning effort"}` — the entire turn is lost. ## Expected Behavior - Every model auto-reports its **real** supported effort levels (from models.dev `reasoning_options`), the picker shows exactly those, and the send path **clamps** any stored value to the nearest supported level — no silent drops, no 400s. - Models whose `reasoning_options` include a `toggle` (e.g. DeepSeek) get the Off switch; models like grok-4.6 that cannot turn thinking off do not. ## Actual Behavior - `grok_supports_reasoning_effort` allowlist in `agent/model_metadata.py` predates grok-4.6 → effort silently dropped. - `agent/transports/codex.py` hard-codes an outdated xAI effort map (folds `xhigh`→`high`; no catalog-driven clamp) → `max`/`ultra` reach the wire and 400. - Picker always renders the full 7-level Hermes scale (`minimal…ultra`) + Off toggle, regardless of the model (this half is being addressed by #85246). ## Live-Verified Effort Matrix (grok-4.6, api.x.ai /v1/responses) | effort | result | |---|---| | minimal / low / medium / high / xhigh | accepted | | max / ultra | **400 Invalid reasoning effort** | | none / thinking.disabled | unsupported — model still reasons | ## Root Cause `agent/model_metadata.py` `grok_supports_reasoning_effort()`: hard-coded model-name allowlist, not updated for grok-4.6. `agent/transports/codex.py`: effort handling has a static xAI-only map; no shared "allowed efforts for this model" concept. Both stem from discarding models.dev `reasoning_options` after parsing only the `reasoning` bool — the exact level list is available in the catalog and thrown away. ## Proposed Fix Data-driven, no hand-maintained allowlist: 1. `agent/models_dev.py`: parse `reasoning_options` into `ModelCapabilities.reasoning_efforts` (filtered to Hermes' scale) + `thinking_off` (has `toggle` / `none`). 2. `hermes_cli/inventory.py` `_apply_capabilities`: carry `reasoning_efforts` / `thinking_off` into the model-options payload (picker side, complements #85246). 3. `agent/models_dev.py` `clamp_reasoning_effort(effort, allowed)`: nearest-neighbor clamp for the send path; unknown models fall back to the full Hermes scale (current behavior). 4. `agent/transports/codex.py`: clamp the wire value to the model's catalog efforts before sending; drop the stale hard-coded xAI map. 5. Desktop picker renders only `reasoning_efforts`, and hides the Off toggle when `thinking_off=false` (complements #85246). Local implementation exists and passes: pytest 108/108 (incl. new `tests/agent/test_reasoning_options.py`), vitest 11/11, `tsc --noEmit` clean. ## Related - #85246 (picker-side filtering — complements this) - #85683 (xAI picker refresh / pin grok-4.6) - #85153 (reasoning_effort: none mishandled for non-reasoning models — same family)
signals.author: PIXYGuo

signals.title: Prefer more official features as plugins to keep Hermes core minimal
signals.text: ## Summary Hermes already shows a strong direction I like: the core stays compact, while platform adapters, business flows, UI panes, and complex skills move into plugins. I would like the team to push this further so the default experience stays simple, and extra capabilities are explicitly opt-in. ## Why - A minimal core is easier to maintain, audit, and run. - Pluginized features can ship, roll back, and evolve independently. - Users can compose only the surfaces they actually need. ## Requested direction 1. Prefer pluginizing platform adapters, message-driven business modes, heavy UI surfaces, and expensive skills. 2. Keep core focused on runtime, sessions, memory, tool protocol, and security boundaries. 3. Make plugin discoverability and enablement clearer in docs and Desktop. ## Examples I like - Hermes-Bot-Mode as a Desktop plugin instead of a core UI change - Telegram Business Mode as an opt-in plugin - Separate plugin/skill/tool packages for heavy integrations ## Impact - Simpler default install - Lower maintenance surface in core - More modular user experience - Clearer upgrade path for optional capabilities
signals.author: HEROISM-WQL

signals.title: [Bug] Hermes Desktop (Linux/Wayland): image paste fails — clipboard image offered as application/octet-stream not recognized
signals.text: ## Bug Description Pasting a screenshot/image into the **Hermes desktop app** fails on a COSMIC/Wayland Linux desktop in every paste method (Ctrl+V, right-click paste, "paste image"), even though the system clipboard correctly holds the image and attaching the same image via the file picker / drag-and-drop works fine. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Press PrtScn (or capture with the COSMIC screenshot tool) to copy a screenshot. 2. Open the Hermes desktop app chat box. 3. Try to attach the image by pasting: Ctrl+V, right-click > paste, or the "+ / paste image" action. 4. Observe: a toast "No image found in clipboard" appears and the image does not attach. 5. As a control: attach the *same* image via the + file picker or drag-and-drop — it attaches correctly. ## Expected Behavior Copying an image (screenshot) to the system clipboard and pasting it into the Hermes desktop chat should attach the image, matching every other modern desktop app. ## Actual Behavior Image pasting fails with "No image found in clipboard"; only manual file attach works. ## Investigation / Root Cause Evidence - System clipboard holds the image fine: `wl-paste --list-types` shows the payload is offered as `application/octet-stream` (not `image/png`), and `wl-paste | od` returns valid PNG magic bytes (`89 50 4e 47`). - Hermes desktop's image-paste path is Electron `clipboard.readImage()` inside the IPC handler `hermes:saveClipboardImage` (`electron/main.ts`). Electron's `readImage()` only recognizes items advertised as `image/png`; an `octet-stream`-offered image returns empty, producing the `noClipboardImage` toast. - A patch adding a `wl-paste --type image/png` (and plain `wl-paste` + PNG-magic) fallback to that handler was built, deployed, and tested on the running app — it did NOT fix paste. This indicates the failure is not isolated to the clipboard-read layer but sits between the renderer paste event and the Electron main-process handler (the renderer's Ctrl+V paste path likely never invokes `saveClipboardImage` for an image-only clipboard). The patch was reverted. - The desktop app does not implement the `/paste` command (that is a CLI/TUI feature), so the documented reliable image-paste path is unavailable on desktop. ## Environment - OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 (COSMIC desktop), Wayland session (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`) - Hermes version: 0.20.0 (desktop app) - Electron main: `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` ## Suggested Direction Investigate the desktop renderer's paste handler (Electron desktop composer) so that a Wayland server offering an image-clipboard item as `application/octet-stream` is still recognized and attached (e.g., a fallback that shells out to `wl-paste` on Linux/Wayland, or broadening the accepted MIME types in `hermes:saveClipboardImage`).
signals.author: jasonswinney7466

signals.title: Custom providers not shared across profiles + no reliable add path in Desktop/CLI
signals.text: ## Summary Adding a custom provider is painful and inconsistent across profiles and surfaces. Three related problems: ### 1. Custom providers are not propagated to other profiles When I add a custom provider in one profile (e.g. `default`), it does **not** appear in my other profiles (`coding-agent`, `telegram`). There is no "apply to all profiles" option. To use the same custom provider everywhere I have to manually copy the `providers:` / `custom_providers:` block and the API key into every profile's `config.yaml` and `.env` by hand. This is error-prone (I ended up with mismatched provider names between profiles) and defeats the purpose of having isolated-but-shareable profiles. Expected: a custom provider added once should be selectable in every profile, or there should be a clear "copy provider to profile X" / "apply to all profiles" action. ### 2. No working way to add a custom provider from Desktop app or CLI - **Desktop app:** the "add custom provider" UI hangs / appears to succeed but then reports the provider is "already added" even when it is not present in the active profile's config. The provider never actually shows up in the model/provider picker. - **CLI:** `hermes config set` cannot be trusted for nested keys — it appends a duplicate top-level block instead of editing the existing key (tracked separately in #71047, still open). So there is no reliable CLI path to add a custom provider to a non-default profile either. Expected: a documented, working flow (`hermes model` picker, `hermes config`, or Desktop settings) to register a custom provider for the *currently active* profile. ### 3. Profile switching itself has open issues Related: #85777 (local profile switch reuses default socket after update) and #71047 (config set duplicates top-level key). Both make the multi-profile experience fragile, which amplifies problem #1. ## Environment - Hermes Agent: current `main` (pyproject ~0.20.x) - Platform: Windows 10 - Profiles: `default`, `coding-agent`, `telegram` - Custom providers involved: `9router` (local OpenAI-compatible endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1`) and `AgentRouter` (`https://agentrouter.org/v1`) ## What I did (manual reproduction of the gap) 1. Registered `9router` + `AgentRouter` in `default` via Desktop app → worked there. 2. Switched to `coding-agent` / `telegram` → neither provider appeared in the picker. 3. Tried adding them again in the Desktop app for the active profile → UI hung / said "already added", nothing written to `config.yaml`. 4. Had to copy `providers:` and `custom_providers:` blocks + `.env` keys manually into each profile's files. ## Suggested improvement - Custom providers should be stored at a shared layer (or have an explicit "share with profile…" control) so they don't have to be re-added per profile. - Fix/provide a reliable add-custom-provider path in both the Desktop app and `hermes model` / `hermes config` (the Desktop "already added" hang and the `config set` duplicate-key bug must be resolved first).
signals.author: zoser69

signals.title: hermes skills update blocked when HERMES_HOME is a Windows junction (physical vs junction path mismatch)
signals.text: ## Summary `hermes skills update` fails for every skill when `HERMES_HOME` lives on a **Windows directory junction** (e.g. `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes` → `D:\hermes`). All updates are blocked by the install-path validation with: ``` Installation blocked: 'D:\hermes\skills\<skill>' is not in the subpath of 'C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills' OR one path is relative and the other is absolute. ``` ## Environment - OS: Windows - Hermes: v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) - Python: 3.11.15 - `HERMES_HOME=C:\Users\xianff\AppData\Local\hermes` is a **junction** → `D:\hermes` ## Root cause When `HERMES_HOME` is a Windows junction, `Path.resolve()` in `_resolve_lock_install_path()` (tools/skills_hub.py) returns the **physical** path (`D:\hermes\skills\<skill>`), but the subsequent `is_relative_to()` / `relative_to()` comparison uses the **junction-form** skills dir (`C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes\skills`). The drive-letter mismatch makes the check fail, so every `hermes skills update` is blocked — even though the skill is already installed and the target is legitimately inside the skills directory. This blocks the **update** path (`hermes skills update`). Related symptom also affects `hermes skills install` for new skills. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Set up `HERMES_HOME` under a Windows directory junction pointing to a physical dir on another drive (e.g. `mklink /J C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\hermes D:\hermes`). 2. Run `hermes skills check` → shows N skills `update_available`. 3. Run `hermes skills update`. 4. Every skill reports `Installation blocked: '<physical path>' is not in the subpath of '<junction path>'`. ## Expected behavior `hermes skills update` should update skills whose directory resolves (via junction/symlink) to a location inside the skills root — the junction is a legitimate filesystem layout, not a path escape. ## Related - PR #76885 "fix(skills): resolve install path against resolved skills dir (Windows junction)" — author's root-cause analysis matches this exactly, but it is **not yet merged** (blocked on requested E2E regression test). - #35674 — symlinked skills trigger false "outside trusted skills directory" warning (same junction/symlink resolution root cause). - #63369 — `hermes skills install` hit the same `subpath of` ValueError on Windows + git-bash.
signals.author: immortal111

signals.title: Add gateway.non_conversational guard for cron-only profiles
signals.text: Hermes supports cron-only gateway processes: a gateway with zero messaging platforms can still tick cron. For security-sensitive scheduled runners, operators need a first-class config option that makes a profile explicitly non-conversational and fails gateway startup if any messaging platform is enabled. Proposed shape: - config: `gateway.non_conversational: true` - startup behavior: before platform adapter creation, if any `platforms.*.enabled=true`, write `startup_failed` runtime status and exit with fatal config code - multiplex behavior: if the default gateway serves a secondary profile with `gateway.non_conversational=true` and any enabled platform, abort multiplexer startup with a config error - use case: split request intake from scheduled execution so conversational agents can record desired alerts while a separate cron-only profile runs them without any chat surface This avoids relying on documentation or systemd `ExecStartPre` alone, both of which are bypassable via direct `hermes --profile <name> gateway run`.
signals.author: michael-renjoy

signals.title: [Bug]: search_files fails on any pattern starting with "-" — missing "--" separator before the pattern (affects both the rg and grep paths)
signals.text: Summary search_files builds its shell command without the -- end-of-options separator before the pattern argument. Any search pattern that begins with - is therefore parsed as a flag by the underlying binary, and the search fails. This is not a quoting problem — _escape_shell_arg correctly wraps the pattern in single quotes, so the shell passes it as one argument. The issue is that rg/grep themselves treat a leading - as an option. The failure is silent from the agent's point of view: the tool returns total_count: 0 with an error string, and in an unattended context (cron job) the run still reports ok, so the model produces an incomplete answer that looks complete. Environment Hermes Agent v0.20.0 (2026.8.3) Install dir: /opt/hermes, Python 3.13.5 Docker (nousresearch/hermes-agent), Debian-based image ripgrep 14.1.1 at /usr/bin/rg (present and working) Reproduction Ask the agent to search for a Markdown task checkbox, which is an extremely common pattern in note vaults: search_files(pattern="- [ ]", path=".", target="content") Result: {"total_count": 0, "error": "Search failed: rg: unrecognized flag - "} Reproduced directly with the exact command shape the tool builds: $ rg --line-number --no-heading --with-filename '- [ ]' . rg: unrecognized flag - $ rg --line-number --no-heading --with-filename -- '- [ ]' . ./notes/Project.md:42:- [ ] pending task The grep fallback has the identical defect: $ grep -rnHE --exclude-dir='.*' '- [ ]' . grep: invalid option -- ' ' $ grep -rnHE --exclude-dir='.*' -- '- [ ]' . ./notes/Project.md:42:- [ ] pending task Root cause tools/file_operations.py, two places, both missing --: 1. _search_with_rg (defined at line 2543), lines 2572-2573: # Add pattern and path cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(pattern)) cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(path)) 2. _search_with_grep (defined at line 2684), lines 2708-2709: identical two lines. Suggested fix Insert the separator immediately before the pattern in both functions: # Add pattern and path. `--` stops option parsing so a pattern that # starts with "-" (e.g. the Markdown checkbox "- [ ]") is not read as a flag. cmd_parts.append("--") cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(pattern)) cmd_parts.append(self._escape_shell_arg(path)) Both rg and GNU grep accept -- in that position, verified above. Impact Any pattern beginning with - is unsearchable. The most common real-world case is the Markdown task checkbox - [ ], plus list items, diff-style lines (-foo), and CLI flags being grepped for in code or logs. The failure mode matters as much as the failure. In a scheduled/cron context there is no user present to notice the tool error, the job still completes with status ok, and the delivered report is quietly missing whatever that search would have found. Workaround Escape the leading character so the pattern no longer starts with - — e.g. search \[ \] instead of - [ ]. This has to be enforced in the prompt, which is fragile: the model will "helpfully" revert to the natural pattern unless it is told why not to.
signals.author: MictlanPro

signals.title: [Bug]: Desktop — single explicit project entry vanishes from sidebar Projects list mid-session; survives restart (backend intact)
signals.text: ## Bug Description While using Hermes Desktop on Windows 11, the **Projects sidebar section stays visible**, but a **single explicit project entry** disappears from the project list **mid-session** — not at startup/re-render. A full desktop-app **restart does not restore** the entry, which points at persisted UI state (localStorage) rather than an in-memory race. ## Environment - Windows 11, Hermes Desktop - Profile: `novel-writer` (single active profile) ## Backend is fully healthy (this is a render-layer bug) - per-profile `projects.db`: project present, `archived=0`, `primary_path` correct (`D:\Hermes_WorkDir\《黑夜将至》-续写`) - `hermes project list` (CLI): shows the project, marked as current (`*`) - `project_list` RPC (desktop plugin): all 3 projects returned; the missing one reported `active=true` - `state.db`: the project's 30+ sessions all present with correct `git_repo_root` So the entry is dropped **only in the rendered tree**, and the dropped state survives restart. ## Related - #67368 — whole PROJECTS section flashes away at init; different symptom, PR #67463 in flight (does NOT cover this path: its root cause is the init toggle race, recoverable by restart) - #85969 — pinned session vanishes; localStorage key missing despite backend `pinned=1`, reload overwrites it (same persistence-flavored mechanism, different UI object) - #64709 (closed) — compression-split sessions lose `cwd`/`git_repo_root` → project sidebar entry disappears on every compression (session-level association, not project-level) ## Notes - Exact trigger action not yet pinned; happens after some time of use. - Happy to run a debug build / capture renderer logs if that helps.
signals.author: vollegrewar

signals.title: bug(desktop): Desktop client broken after last 2 updates on Windows — backend exits (1), cannot restart itself, WinError 32 lock chain
signals.text: ## Summary The Hermes **desktop client** on Windows is broken after the last **2 consecutive updates** (2026-07-31 and 2026-08-14). After each update the desktop app's backend exits with code 1, the app can't restart itself ("Reopen Hermes to finish"), and the update pipeline falls back through git → ZIP, both of which fail on `WinError 32` file locks. The app only comes back after manually closing and reopening it. This is the desktop-app variant of the Windows update lock chain already tracked in #63717 and #68760, but with an additional failure: the desktop update hand-off finishes with a **manual action** instead of restarting the app, and the backend repeatedly exits (1) during the update window. ## Environment - **OS:** Windows 11 (git-bash/MSYS shell) - **Hermes:** git install at `C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent` (venv), branch main, HEAD `de0abc061` (2026-08-14) - **Desktop build stamp:** `desktop-build-stamp.json` builtAt 2026-08-14T08:43:15Z, sourceMode=false - **Python:** 3.11.15 (venv), uv 0.12.0 (managed) - **Update dates:** 2026-07-31 00:38, 2026-08-14 16:41 and 23:57 (two attempts on the 14th) ## What happened (from `~/.hermes/logs/`) ### 1. Desktop backend exits (1) repeatedly during the update window `desktop.log`: ``` [hermes] [updates] restart: Updating Hermes — this window will close and the updater will open. Don't reopen Hermes yourself; it restarts automatically when the update finishes. [hermes] [updates] state.db pre-flight: size=175353856, headerOk=true, ... [hermes] [updates] venv shim unlocked; safe to proceed [hermes] Hermes backend exited (1) [hermes] [boot] An update is finishing — Hermes will start automatically when it completes… [hermes] [updates] launched repo hand-off script: ...\scripts\desktop-update\windows.ps1 (branch main); exiting desktop to release venv shim [hermes] [updates] detached update finished with manual action (branch main): Update complete. Reopen Hermes to finish (it could not restart itself). ``` The same `Hermes backend exited (1)` line appears ~10 times across the two update events; the app does **not** restart itself after the update completes — the user has to manually close and reopen it every time. ### 2. `hermes update` fails: git install → ZIP fallback → both hit WinError 32 `update.log` (2026-08-14 16:41): ``` ⚠ hermes.exe is locked by another process; scheduled replacement on next reboot. error: failed to remove file `...\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages\../../Scripts/hermes.exe`: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32) ⚠ Git update failed: Command '[...\uv.exe', 'pip', 'install', '-e', '.']' returned non-zero exit status 2. → Falling back to ZIP download... ✗ ZIP update failed: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: '...\hermes-agent\ui-tui' -> '...\hermes-agent\ui-tui.hermes-update-old' ``` Same pattern in `hermes-update.log` (2026-07-31): `hermes.exe` locked by another process (os error 32) → git update failed → ZIP fallback → `WinError 32` on `ui-tui` rename. ### 3. Secondary noise during boot `desktop.log`: ``` [hermes] [boot] could not read served dashboard token (Hermes backend): 404: {"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled — use `hermes dashboard` for the browser UI."} ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: TERMINAL_CWD=... (move to config.yaml terminal.cwd) ``` ## Expected behavior - `hermes update` / desktop self-update completes on Windows **without** WinError 32 lock failures (detect/kill the processes holding `hermes.exe` and `.pyd`/`ui-tui` files, or use a staged/reboot-safe replacement). - The desktop app restarts itself after the detached update finishes instead of requiring a manual reopen ("it could not restart itself"). - No `Hermes backend exited (1)` during the update hand-off window. ## Workaround used Close the desktop app fully, run the update, then manually reopen — works, but every update requires this manual dance and the ZIP fallback still leaves a partially-updated tree. ## Related - #63717 — Windows: Hermes Desktop update failures (comprehensive diagnostic, 7 correlated root causes) - #68760 — hermes.exe locked during `hermes update` on Windows (WinError 32)
signals.author: aKa368

signals.title: sessions recover --inspect-only can miss malformed canonical payload pages
signals.text: ## Bug Description On current `main` (`de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe`), `hermes sessions recover --inspect-only` can report `recoverable: true` when a required canonical table's payload B-tree is malformed. The inspection path treats `PRAGMA table_info(...)` plus `SELECT COUNT(*)` as proof that a table is completely readable. SQLite may satisfy `COUNT(*)` from a healthy covering index without touching damaged table payload pages. Strict recovery later selects the payload columns and fails. This makes `--inspect-only` a false health signal precisely in the corruption case it is intended to diagnose. ## Steps to Reproduce I reproduced this with a synthetic SQLite fixture against the upstream commit above; no user database or private content is involved. 1. Create one session with 320 messages whose payloads are 1,500 bytes each. 2. Checkpoint, switch to `journal_mode=DELETE`, and `VACUUM` so the `messages` table spans multiple leaves. 3. Confirm that SQLite plans `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages` through the covering index `idx_messages_session_id`. 4. Corrupt the two-byte cell-count field beginning at page-header offset 3 of one middle `messages` **table** leaf, while leaving `idx_messages_session_id` untouched. The synthetic fixture and exact corrupting edit are included in PR #86237. 5. Run `inspect_session_database(source)` (the implementation behind `--inspect-only`). 6. Run strict `recover_session_database(source, output)`. Observed fixture facts: ```text count query plan: SCAN messages USING COVERING INDEX idx_messages_session_id count result: 320 SELECT * FROM messages: database disk image is malformed inspect tables.messages.rows: 320 inspect recoverable: true strict messages copy status: failed strict messages copied_rows: 0 strict messages error: database disk image is malformed strict recovery complete: false strict recovery verified: false ``` ## Expected Behavior Inspection should traverse the canonical payload projection that strict recovery needs, using bounded memory. A malformed required-table payload should not produce `recoverable: true` merely because a secondary index can answer `COUNT(*)`. At minimum, the per-table inspection result should distinguish count/index readability from payload readability. Ideally the top-level report should also distinguish required-session salvageability from strict all-canonical-table recoverability. ## Actual Behavior `_table_inventory()` records a table as available and readable after: ```python columns = _table_columns(conn, table) result["rows"] = int( conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{table}"').fetchone()[0] ) ``` `_inspect_connection()` then declares the source recoverable when the `sessions` and `messages` counts are non-null. No payload row is read during inspection. ## Affected Component CLI (`hermes sessions recover --inspect-only`) / session-state recovery. ## Messaging Platform N/A (offline CLI recovery). ## Debug Report Not uploaded: this is a deterministic synthetic corruption fixture on current upstream `main`, with no live configuration, credentials, logs, session text, or user database. All relevant aggregate output is included above. ## Operating System Linux 6.8.0-63-generic x86_64 ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version `main@de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe` (`v2026.8.13-106-gde0abc0617`) ## Root Cause Analysis `hermes_cli/session_recovery.py::_table_inventory()` uses `SELECT COUNT(*)` as its only row-read probe. SQLite is free to answer that query from a covering index. Damage confined to table leaves or overflow pages is therefore not touched until `_copy_table()` executes `SELECT <all compatible columns> FROM <table>`. This is separate from: - #80205, which addressed `--allow-partial` rowid range-budget exhaustion; - #80255, which concerns the WAL `TRUNCATE` checkpoint shutdown corruption path; - #32687, which predates the current offline recovery command. Related but distinct: #86236 concerns silent omission of durable auxiliary state after source payloads are readable. ## Proposed Fix - Stream the canonical table's full column projection for `--inspect-only` rather than treating `COUNT(*)` as a payload-readability proof. - Use `NOT INDEXED` so a healthy secondary index cannot mask malformed payload pages, and so a damaged rebuildable secondary index does not create a false negative for table data. - Count rows during that streaming scan instead of materializing the table in memory. - Keep the normal recovery pre-copy inventory lightweight; strict recovery already reads every payload during copy, so it should not double-scan large databases. - Record payload-read errors explicitly in the per-table report. - Add a physical SQLite regression fixture that corrupts a table leaf while preserving the covering count index. ## PR willingness Focused regression PR: #86237.
signals.author: noodle-bag

signals.title: sessions recover reports complete after omitting durable auxiliary state
signals.text: ## Bug Description On current `main` (`de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe`), `hermes sessions recover` can report all of the following: ```text complete: true verified: true verification.loss_detected: false verification.errors: [] verification.warnings: [] ``` while silently omitting durable state from the source database: 1. the entire lazy-created `delivery_obligations` table, including non-terminal owed replies; and 2. source-only columns added by lazy schema migration, demonstrated by a non-empty `async_delegations.origin_session_id` value. The dangerous outbox case is not that terminal `delivered` rows are necessarily required forever; it is that non-terminal obligations (`pending`, `attempting`, `failed` — everything outside the pruned `delivered`/`abandoned` set) can disappear without any recovery warning. The terminal-row retention policy can remain a maintainer decision. ## Steps to Reproduce This was reproduced with a synthetic fixture against the upstream commit above; no live user database or private message content is involved. 1. Create a fresh `SessionDB` with one session and one message. 2. Initialize the current delivery-ledger schema with `gateway.delivery_ledger._initialize_schema()`. 3. Initialize the current async-delegation lazy schema with `tools.async_delegation._initialize_schema()`. 4. Insert: - one `delivery_obligations` row in `pending` state; - one row in `delivered` state; - one `async_delegations` row whose `origin_session_id` is non-empty. 5. Run strict `recover_session_database(source, output)`. 6. Inspect the output schema and recovery report. Actual recovery-report fields: ```json { "complete": true, "verified": true, "verification": { "loss_detected": false, "errors": [], "warnings": [] } } ``` The synthetic harness separately observed that the source contained one `pending` and one `delivered` obligation, the destination had no `delivery_obligations` table, the source had `async_delegations.origin_session_id`, and the destination did not. These are harness observations, not keys emitted by `recover_session_database()`. The recovered `async_delegations` row exists, but its source-only `origin_session_id` column and value do not. ## Expected Behavior A recovery output must not be reported as complete and lossless when non-terminal durable delivery obligations or non-default source-only canonical columns were omitted. At minimum, the recovery report should: - inventory relevant auxiliary durable tables; - list omitted source tables and source-only columns; - detect whether omitted columns contain non-null/non-default values; - set `loss_detected: true` and `complete: false` when durable data was omitted; - warn explicitly about non-terminal delivery obligations that were not preserved. The eventual data-preservation policy can be handled separately: - whether to copy every obligation or only non-terminal rows; - whether recovered owner PID stamps should be cleared/reassigned; - whether lazy initializers should move into the base schema or be registered with recovery. ## Actual Behavior `recover_session_database()` initializes the destination only through base `SessionDB`, then copies a fixed canonical table list. `_copy_table()` selects only the intersection of destination and source columns: ```python source_columns = _table_columns(source, table) destination_columns = _table_columns(destination, table) columns = [column for column in destination_columns if column in source_columns] ``` The copy is marked `complete` when copied row count equals source row count, even if source-only columns with non-empty values were dropped. `delivery_obligations` is not inventoried or copied at all. The destination does not initialize that lazy table, and the report emits no omission warning. ## Affected Component CLI (`hermes sessions recover`) / session-state recovery / gateway durability ledger. ## Messaging Platform N/A for reproduction. The omitted obligations can belong to any gateway platform. ## Debug Report Not uploaded: this is a deterministic synthetic fixture on current upstream `main`. It contains only placeholder strings and no configuration, credentials, logs, platform identifiers, or user data. ## Operating System Linux 6.8.0-63-generic x86_64 ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version `main@de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe` (`v2026.8.13-106-gde0abc0617`) ## Root Cause Analysis There are two related completeness gaps: 1. **Fixed recovery inventory:** `delivery_obligations` is created lazily in `gateway/delivery_ledger.py` and is absent from the recovery table set. 2. **Schema intersection without loss accounting:** base `hermes_state_common.py` creates `async_delegations` without `origin_session_id`; `tools/async_delegation.py` adds it lazily. Recovery initializes only the base schema, copies common columns, compares row counts, and reports the table complete. This is separate from open PR #67078, which addresses live gateway crash/replay semantics rather than offline `state.db` recovery. Related but distinct: #86224 concerns `--inspect-only` failing to traverse malformed canonical payload pages. ## Proposed Fix First, make the report honest without prematurely deciding replay semantics: - record omitted tables and source-only columns; - inspect whether omitted data is materially populated; - classify populated omissions as loss; - report non-terminal delivery-obligation state counts and fail closed or warn prominently. Follow-up preservation work can then initialize current runtime schemas and copy/reconcile obligations under a maintainer-approved replay policy. ## PR willingness Focused reporting PR: #86245. The actual obligation-preservation policy remains a separate follow-up after maintainer confirmation.
signals.author: noodle-bag

signals.title: [Bug]: anthropic_messages and chat.completions omit a session continuity header, so a session-aware proxy replays the whole history every turn
signals.text: ## Bug description Hermes sends no per-conversation continuity header on the `anthropic_messages` and OpenAI-compatible chat-completions transports. When a custom provider is a session-aware proxy, it has nothing to correlate requests with, and an agent loop degrades into one fresh upstream conversation per turn. This is the same family as #65094 (custom Codex-compatible `/v1` providers omit Hermes session headers) but a different transport and a different failure shape. #65094 concerns `ResponsesApiTransport` gating headers behind `is_codex_backend`. This one concerns the two remaining send sites, where no session header is constructed at all. ## Why it bites specifically here A proxy that fronts a stateful backend has to decide per request whether it continues an existing conversation or starts a new one. With no id to key on, it falls back to heuristics. The one measured here classifies a request as independent when it carries no session id and its **last message is a `tool_result`**: ```js isClientDrivenLoop = adapterBase !== "claude-code" && !agentSessionId && lastIsToolResult ``` Nearly every request in an agent loop ends in a `tool_result`, so nearly every request was treated as a new conversation and the entire message history was re-sent upstream. ## Measurements Single machine, four Claude seats on `api_mode: anthropic_messages` through a local proxy. Proxy telemetry, 77 requests: | lineage | requests | cache_write | share of write | |---|---:|---:|---:| | new | 69 (90%) | 3,155,137 | 91% | | continuation | 6 | 210,012 | 6% | | undo / compaction | 2 | 109,023 | 3% | The `new` requests show the signature clearly — `cache_read` pinned at the static system+tools floor no matter how long the conversation is, while `cache_write` scales with it: ``` messages= 3 cache_write= 38,724 cache_read=20,311 messages= 7 cache_write= 60,067 cache_read=20,311 messages=13 cache_write=102,323 cache_read=20,311 ``` The few requests that did correlate show the intended shape: 39 messages, `cache_write` 452, `cache_read` 100,431. Day totals on that machine were cache_read 5,398,004 / cache_write 5,494,827 — roughly 1:1. A workload that reuses its prefix should read far more than it writes, and that near-parity is what first suggested the split was not workload-shaped. ## Fix Attach a header carrying a value that is stable within a session and distinct between sessions — `agent.session_id` already has exactly that lifetime — read at request time so it does not depend on client lifetime or on one gateway process serving many sessions. Send sites that need it: - `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — `request_client.chat.completions.create()` (streaming and non-streaming) - `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` — `request_client.messages.stream()` - `run_agent.py` — `_anthropic_messages_create` Two notes from doing it: 1. **Patching only the OpenAI-compatible sites changes nothing for Claude seats.** Measured after that first attempt: `new` 85%, against 90% before. Those seats set `api_mode: anthropic_messages` and never reach those sites. 2. **A shared constant would be worse than sending nothing.** Every session would match one lineage and be read as a rewritten history rather than a new one. ## After ``` 02:10:01 new 35 msg write 54,306 read 0 <- establishes the lineage 02:10:07 continuation 37 msg write 2,804 read 54,306 02:10:16 continuation 39 msg write 1,194 read 57,110 02:10:21 continuation 41 msg write 1,496 read 58,304 ``` `cache_read` now grows with the conversation and `cache_write` stays small. The remaining `new` requests were legitimate session establishment — the first request after a restart, and the first request of a resumed older session. ## Scope The heuristic quoted above belongs to that proxy, not to Hermes. But the condition it keys on — no session id, last message is a `tool_result` — is what an OpenAI-format agent client looks like by default, so any comparable proxy has the same decision to make. Sending the id is the client-side half.
signals.author: VerumRex3

signals.title: [Bug]: kanban tool output is inflated twice over — ensure_ascii escaping and an unconditional worker_context
signals.text: ## Bug description Two unrelated things make `tools/kanban_tools.py` return far more than it carries. Neither is fixable by how a seat uses the board. ## 1. `json.dumps` without `ensure_ascii=False` All four call sites that produce tool output escape non-Latin characters, so each one becomes a six-byte `\uXXXX` sequence. On a board written in Japanese that is most of the response. One `kanban_show` result, measured: ``` output 59,598 chars \uXXXX sequences 6,265 -> 37,590 chars (63.1%) with ensure_ascii=False 28,273 chars (2.11x inflation) ``` Across 82 recent kanban tool results: **1,995,547 -> 1,149,517 characters**, so 846,030 characters (42%) carried no information. Every other tool surface in the tree already passes `ensure_ascii=False` — `browser_tool.py`, `browser_cdp_tool.py`, and others. Kanban looks like the exception rather than a deliberate choice. Affected: `_ok()`, `_handle_show`, `_handle_list`, `_handle_attachments`. The two `json.dumps` calls that round-trip through `json.loads` for redaction are internal and do not need changing. ## 2. `kanban_show` attaches `worker_context` to every caller `worker_context` is built by `kb.build_worker_context()` and re-renders the title, body, prior attempts and comment thread as prose — the same content the response already carries as structured fields. For the worker it is essential and must stay. `_default_spawn` launches a worker with `prompt = f"work kanban task {task.id}"` and nothing else (`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py`), and `KANBAN_GUIDANCE` tells it to call `kanban_show()` first and treat `worker_context` as ground truth. It is that worker's only orientation channel. For an orchestrator reading the board it is pure duplication. Measured on one card, it was **28,941 of 59,598 characters (48.6%)** — re-sent on every board read. The caller is already identifiable: `_check_kanban_mode` distinguishes a dispatcher-spawned worker via `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` plus `_is_dispatcher_owned_worker()`. Gating the block on the caller being the worker **for that specific task** keeps the worker's payload byte-identical (modulo the escaping fix) and drops it for everyone else. ## Combined effect Same card, all three caller paths measured: | caller | before | after | | |---|---:|---:|---:| | orchestrator | 64,659 | 16,311 | -74.8% | | worker on another card | 64,659 | 16,311 | -74.8% | | **worker on its own card** | 64,659 | 30,294 | -53.1%, content unchanged | `tests/tools/test_kanban_tools.py::test_show_defaults_to_env_task_id` covers the worker path and still passes — its fixture sets `HERMES_KANBAN_TASK` to the card under test. The orchestrator path had no coverage before.
signals.author: VerumRex3

signals.title: Desktop: sameCronSignature drops pin/archive-only session updates
signals.text: ## Bug On current `main`, Desktop session refreshes discard pages whose only changes are row-state flags. `sameCronSignature()` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/session-signatures.ts` compares content and recency fields, but not `pinned` or `archived`. `refreshSessions()` therefore keeps the previous atom when a fetched page changes only one of those flags: ```ts return sameCronSignature(prev, next) ? prev : next ``` The backend write succeeds, but `$sessions` can retain the stale row indefinitely for an idle conversation. For pinning, that stale row is then consumed by `session-pin-sync`; once its confirmation guard expires, an old `pinned: true` row can resurrect an item the user already unpinned. The same omission makes archive-only changes invisible to this signature gate. ## Distinct from earlier pin races This is not the earlier pull-before-push race fixed by #75973 for #74570. It is also one layer above the write-confirmation guard added by #77170 for #76919: the guard has a valid confirmation path, but the page carrying the confirming `pinned` value is filtered out before it can reach the reconciler. ## Reproduction 1. Start with an idle pinned conversation, so no title, preview, count, or timestamp field is moving. 2. Unpin it and confirm the backend row changes to `pinned = 0`. 3. Let session refresh return the same row with only `pinned` changed. 4. The page is judged signature-equal and discarded; the cached row remains `pinned: true`. After the write guard expires, a later reconciliation can re-adopt that stale value. A focused unit test that changes only `pinned` fails on current `main`; the equivalent archive-only test fails as well. ## Expected behavior `sameCronSignature()` should treat both `pinned` and `archived` as significant row state, with regression tests for pin-only and archive-only deltas. This causes one atom update per deliberate pin or archive action and does not reintroduce ordinary session-page churn. ## Proposed fix PR #86218 implements the minimal fix and regression coverage: - compare `session.pinned === other.pinned` - compare `session.archived === other.archived` - add pin-only, archive-only, and unchanged-state tests No additional `session-pin-sync` retry behavior is required for this issue unless a fresh reproduction remains after the confirming page is allowed through.
signals.author: james47kjv

signals.title: Relay-fronted cron delivery: out-of-process runs have no transport (relay registers no standalone_sender_fn) — scheduled reports never reach Discord on Hermes Cloud
signals.text: Scheduled cron jobs on a relay-fronted deployment (Hermes Cloud instance behind the Team Gateway connector) execute fine but never deliver: every run ends with `platform 'discord' not configured/enabled`. The in-process path for this exact topology works and is tested; the gap is that Chronos-triggered cron runs execute out-of-process, and the relay platform registers no `standalone_sender_fn`, so out-of-process delivery has no transport at all. ## Environment - Hermes Cloud instance (always-on), relay-only: `config.yaml` `platforms:` contains only the `relay` block, no native `discord` credentials (by design — the connector holds the bot token). - Interactive traffic works perfectly: inbound DMs and replies ride the live gateway's relay websocket. - Cron jobs created from the Discord DM session with `deliver=origin` (`origin.platform=discord`). ## Symptom Every scheduled run: agent executes, report is written to disk, then ``` WARNING cron.scheduler: Job 'c588c14f3abf': platform 'discord' not configured/enabled ``` `last_status: ok`, `last_delivery_error: platform 'discord' not configured/enabled`. Same for `hermes cron run <id>` from a shell. Execution records show `source=chronos` — the runs are triggered out-of-process relative to the live gateway. ## Diagnosis (source at head) 1. Out-of-process delivery resolves through the standalone path, which requires the platform's `PlatformEntry.standalone_sender_fn` (`tools/send_message_tool.py:747`, error string at `:778`). 2. Discord's native plugin registers one (`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:10147`) — but a relay-only deployment has no native Discord config, so the logical-platform lookup fails first. 3. The relay platform's own `PlatformEntry` registers **no** `standalone_sender_fn` (`gateway/relay/__init__.py:955-965` — `adapter_factory`, `check_fn`, no standalone hook). Probing `deliver=relay:<chat_id>` directly confirms: ``` delivery error: No live adapter for platform 'relay'. Is the gateway running with this platform connected? For out-of-process delivery (e.g. cron in a separate process), the platform plugin must register a standalone_sender_fn on its PlatformEntry. ``` 4. The **in-process** path handles this topology correctly and is pinned by tests: `tests/cron/test_relay_fronted_delivery.py::TestRelayDeliveryGate::test_relay_fronted_platform_is_not_rejected` ("a live relay transport that fronts Discord must deliver even though platforms.discord has no native config block at all"), plus the preflight guard in `tests/cron/test_cron_relay_delivery_guards.py`. So fire-time routing via `resolve_delivery_transport` + `fronts_platform` is all there — it just never runs, because on Hermes Cloud the scheduler executing the job is not the gateway process. Net effect: on a relay-only hosted instance, every out-of-process cron delivery target except `local` fails identically, while the same job's delivery would succeed if executed inside the gateway process. ## Fix options (design call, hence issue not PR) 1. **`standalone_sender_fn` for the relay platform**: dial the connector, handshake, send one egress frame, close. Caveat that makes this non-obvious: the connector treats a new handshake as a resume trigger (`gateway/relay/__init__.py` transport comment: re-handshake triggers the buffered-flip drain), and the live gateway already holds a socket for the same gateway identity — a second concurrent socket may disrupt it. If the connector multiplexes per-connection rather than per-gateway-id this is safe; that's connector-semantics knowledge a maintainer has and I don't. 2. **Loopback IPC to the live gateway**: the standalone sender POSTs to the local gateway's API server and the live process sends via its existing relay socket. No second socket, no handshake question; adds an API-server route (or reuses one if a send route already exists). 3. **Chronos-side**: for always-on instances, have the Chronos trigger hand execution to the gateway process (in-process scheduler), where delivery already works. Scale-to-zero instances still need (1) or (2) for the wake-up case. Happy to build whichever direction is preferred — (2) looks safest from outside, but the connector team knows whether (1)'s second socket is harmless. ## Repro Any relay-only deployment: create a cron job with `deliver=origin` from a Discord session fronted by the connector, let it fire, read `last_delivery_error`.
signals.author: SHL0MS

signals.title: [Bug] Desktop: secondary profile's pooled serve is spawned but its WebSocket is never dialed — sidebar shows primary profile's project tree
signals.text: ## Summary Desktop app v0.20.1 (macOS, LOCAL mode, 2+ profiles): switching to a non-primary profile spawns that profile's pooled backend serve, but the renderer **never establishes a WebSocket connection to it**. The sidebar project tree therefore falls back to the last-known tree of the PRIMARY profile. Clicking any primary-profile project inside the secondary profile's view auto-switches the app back to the primary profile. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Have 2+ local profiles (primary + secondary) with distinct projects. 2. Open the app; the primary tree renders in the sidebar. 3. Switch to the secondary profile via the rail. 4. Observed: the sidebar STILL shows the primary profile's projects (project-tree grouping). The secondary profile's own projects never appear. 5. Click any primary-profile project → the app switches the active profile back to primary (pill changes) and opens the session. 6. Workaround found: switching sidebar grouping to **"updated"** (recent) shows the secondary profile's sessions correctly — that list path IS profile-scoped. So session data routing is fine; only the project tree is wrong. ## Evidence - Fresh app restart, 3 serves spawned at boot: - primary serve: holds the app's ESTABLISHED connections (2). - secondary serve: spawned as `--profile <secondary> serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`, LISTENING on its ephemeral port, but **0 ESTABLISHED connections** from the app (`lsof -nP -a -p <pid> -iTCP`). - External WS probe of the secondary serve + `projects.tree` returns the CORRECT tree (its own projects only). The backend is healthy; the renderer just never dials it. - Persists across full app restarts (Cmd+Q), not just a reload. Not the all-profiles browse mode (`hermes.desktop.showAllProfiles` = false in localStorage). ## Expected behavior Switching to a profile shows that profile's own project tree in the sidebar. ## Environment - macOS 15.7.5 (arm64), Hermes Desktop v0.20.1 - Local profiles only, no remote gateway / no per-profile connection overrides ## Code trail (source at current HEAD) - `apps/desktop/src/store/profile.ts` — `selectProfile()` → `ensureGatewayProfile(name)` - `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts` — `ensureGatewayForProfile()` → `openSecondary()` → `desktop.getConnection(profile)` → `entry.gateway.connect(wsUrl)`; on failure `scheduleReconnect(entry)` runs and `setActive(key)` STILL executes, so `$activeGatewayProfile` moves to the secondary profile while its socket is dead. - `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — `ensureBackend()` returns the pooled `connectionPromise`; `spawnPoolBackend()` self-probes `/api/ws` before declaring ready, so the descriptor looks valid. - `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` — `refreshProjectTree()` → `activeProjectsContext()` → `activeGateway()`; with a dead secondary gateway the refresh fails and the cached (primary) tree is kept by design ("failure leaves the cached tree intact so the sidebar doesn't flicker"). ## Possibly related - #77005 (remote mode, same symptom family: sidebar shows launch profile's projects) - #75308 (projects_db_path per-profile) - #74551 (wrong profile backend after reconnect)

signals.title: Desktop: show owning profile in flat All Profiles recents
signals.text: ## Problem Hermes Desktop's **All Profiles** sidebar can show ordinary recent sessions from several profiles in one flat chronological list. Unlike pinned sessions and search results, these ordinary rows do not show their owning profile. This becomes especially ambiguous when several profiles use the same canonical session title (for example, Bot Mode profiles commonly use `Bot Chat`). The status dot is not sufficient because it communicates session state, not profile identity. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure two or more named Hermes profiles. 2. Create or open sessions under those profiles. 3. Select **All Profiles** in Hermes Desktop. 4. Keep the Sessions sidebar in its flat/date-grouped view rather than grouping by Profile. ## Current behavior Ordinary recent-session rows display their title and status but not the owning profile. Identical titles cannot be distinguished without opening the sessions. ## Expected behavior In flat **All Profiles** recents: - Show the existing profile identity glyph for named-profile session rows. - Preserve the glyph's tooltip and accessible label (`Profile: <name>`). - Do not show redundant per-row glyphs when sessions are grouped by Profile. - Do not change scoped/single-profile views. - Leave existing pinned and search-result behavior unchanged. ## Notes This extends the ownership treatment introduced for pinned/search rows in #66003 / #66449 to ordinary flat recents. It does not rename sessions or change routing, persistence, or Bot Mode protocol. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop 0.20.1 - macOS 26.5.2 - Multiple profiles viewed through All Profiles
