signal.title: feat(gateway): dump wedged worker stacks when the turn reaper fires
signal.text: ## Summary When the gateway's inactivity reaper fires on a timed-out turn, it now dumps the wedged worker thread's stack to the log BEFORE interrupting — so the next zombie-turn incident names the exact blocked frame instead of destroying the evidence. Root cause context (Aug 2026 live incident): a WhatsApp session wedged EVERY turn for exactly the 1800s inactivity timeout. The conversation loop finished in ~3s each time ("Turn ended: reason=text_response"), then the worker thread blocked somewhere in post-turn finalization until the reaper's hard interrupt freed it ("response ready: time=1810.8s"). Corroborating signals pointed at a Relay-corrupted scope stack ("Skipping Relay instrumentation for concurrent Hermes turn", shutdown error "scope handle is not at the top of the stack") — but the exact blocked frame was unprovable post-mortem, because the interrupt that surfaces the problem also releases the frame. This PR closes that observability gap; the actual wedge fix follows once a dump names the frame. Companion to #85968 (which makes restarts immune to wedged turns). ## Changes - `gateway/run.py`: `_dump_wedged_turn_stacks()` — walks `sys._current_frames()`, logs stacks of threads containing turn-machinery frames (`run_sync`, `end_turn`, `run_in_session`, `finalize_turn`, …). Bounded (max 8 threads, last 25 frames each), pure in-process, never raises into the reaper. Called from `_abandon_timed_out_gateway_turn()` before `request_hard_interrupt`. - `tests/gateway/test_abandoned_turn_process_cleanup.py`: 3 new tests — a real blocked thread is captured with its blocking line named; dump ordering (dump → interrupt → reap); dump never raises even when frame walking fails. ## Validation | | Result | |---|---| | New + existing reaper tests | 11/11 passed | | + inactivity-timeout + restart-drain suites | 26 passed, 2 skipped | | Sabotage run (dump call removed) | ordering test FAILS — proves coverage | | Real-thread test | dump names `run_sync` frame AND the exact blocked line (`release.wait`) | ## Infographic ![Catch the freeze in the act](https://files.catbox.moe/q2jw34.png)
signal.author: teknium1

signal.title: fix(gateway): exclude wedged turns from the restart after-turn wait; default cap 6h -> 30min
signal.text: ## Summary `hermes update` / `hermes gateway restart` no longer blocks for hours behind a turn that is already dead — wedged turns (idle past `agent.gateway_timeout`) are excluded from the restart after-turn wait, and the shipped `restart_after_turn_timeout` default drops from 6h to 30min (#79133). Root cause: the #77184 graceful-restart path waits for all `_active_work_count()` to reach zero before `stop()`, capped at `restart_after_turn_timeout` (default 21600s). A wedged agent — one the gateway's own inactivity watchdog had already declared dead ("Agent idle for 1803s" errors every 30 min) — still counted as active work, so the drain waited on it for the full cap. Live incident (Aug 2026): a WhatsApp turn idle 30+ min pinned `hermes update` in "draining (up to 21675s)" until a manual SIGTERM. ## Changes - `gateway/run.py`: new `_wedged_agent_count()` — running agents whose `get_activity_summary()` reports inactivity ≥ `agent.gateway_timeout` (same threshold as the turn reaper). `_await_active_work_before_restart()` waits on `_awaitable_work_count()` (active minus wedged) instead of all active work; all-wedged short-circuits straight to `stop()`, whose bounded drain (`restart_drain_timeout`) interrupts them. - `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`: `restart_after_turn_timeout` 21600 → 1800 (salvaged from #80321 by @thatssoheil, closes #79133) — the 6h cap only ever mattered in the wedged case, where it is indistinguishable from "no cap" for an operator at a terminal. - Safety: `gateway_timeout=0` (operator opted into unbounded turns) disables wedge detection; cron/API-server work has no per-turn activity clock and is never counted wedged; pending sentinels and unreadable summaries fail open (not wedged). Live turns are still honored — mixed live+wedged waits for the live turn only. ## Validation | Scenario | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Only wedged turn active, restart requested | drain waits full after-turn cap (6h default) | proceeds to stop() immediately; bounded 60s drain interrupts it | | Live + wedged turns | waits on both | waits on live only, wedged excluded | | `gateway_timeout=0` | n/a | wedge detection disabled, cap still bounds wait | | Sabotage run (fix reverted) | — | both new regression tests FAIL (TimeoutError), proving they exercise the bug | `tests/gateway/test_restart_drain.py` + `test_restart_after_turn.py` + cron/API drain suites: 40 passed, 2 skipped. ## Infographic ![Restart never waits on a dead turn](https://files.catbox.moe/m4mqwz.png)

signal.title: gateway: restart_after_turn_timeout default of 21600s (6h) makes interactive gateway restarts effectively unbounded when a turn wedges
signal.text: ## Summary `config_defaults.py` ships `agent.restart_after_turn_timeout: 21600` (6 hours), introduced in db3f7e4eb (#77184). Combined with `resolve_restart_exit_wait_budget()` (`gateway/restart.py`), an interactive `hermes gateway restart` prints: ``` ⏳ User service restarting gracefully (PID …) — waiting up to 21675s for in-flight turns + drain... ``` 21675 = 21600 (after-turn default) + 60 (drain, local config) + 15 (headroom). ## Why this is a footgun The intent of #77184 is sound — don't force-kill an agent mid-turn. And when the gateway is idle the restart is immediate, so most users never see the cap. But the cap only *matters* in exactly one scenario: a turn that never finishes (hung tool call, wedged event loop, stuck provider stream). In that scenario: - An operator who typed `hermes gateway restart` at a terminal watches the CLI block for **up to six hours** before the fallback path engages. - The natural human response is Ctrl-C plus a manual `systemctl kill` — i.e. exactly the ungraceful kill #77184 was written to avoid, now performed by an annoyed human with less care. - Restart is often the *remedy* for a wedged turn; a 6h deferral means the remedy waits on the disease. A cap this long is indistinguishable from "no cap" for interactive use, while long enough to mask genuinely stuck sessions (cf. #66892, a 26h zombie). ## Suggested fix Lower the default to something in the 15–30 minute range (e.g. `900`–`1800`). That still protects the overwhelming majority of long autonomous turns (tool calls have their own timeouts well below that), while keeping worst-case interactive restart latency in human-tolerable territory. Users running very long unattended turns can raise it in `config.yaml` — that's the right place for a 6h opt-in, rather than the default every install inherits. No code change needed beyond the one literal in `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` (plus doc mention); the resolution chain already honors config/env overrides. ## Environment - Observed on v0.20.0, Linux/systemd user service.

signal.title: bug(desktop): Desktop client broken after last 2 updates on Windows — backend exits (1), cannot restart itself, WinError 32 lock chain
signal.text: ## Summary The Hermes **desktop client** on Windows is broken after the last **2 consecutive updates** (2026-07-31 and 2026-08-14). After each update the desktop app's backend exits with code 1, the app can't restart itself ("Reopen Hermes to finish"), and the update pipeline falls back through git → ZIP, both of which fail on `WinError 32` file locks. The app only comes back after manually closing and reopening it. This is the desktop-app variant of the Windows update lock chain already tracked in #63717 and #68760, but with an additional failure: the desktop update hand-off finishes with a **manual action** instead of restarting the app, and the backend repeatedly exits (1) during the update window. ## Environment - **OS:** Windows 11 (git-bash/MSYS shell) - **Hermes:** git install at `C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent` (venv), branch main, HEAD `de0abc061` (2026-08-14) - **Desktop build stamp:** `desktop-build-stamp.json` builtAt 2026-08-14T08:43:15Z, sourceMode=false - **Python:** 3.11.15 (venv), uv 0.12.0 (managed) - **Update dates:** 2026-07-31 00:38, 2026-08-14 16:41 and 23:57 (two attempts on the 14th) ## What happened (from `~/.hermes/logs/`) ### 1. Desktop backend exits (1) repeatedly during the update window `desktop.log`: ``` [hermes] [updates] restart: Updating Hermes — this window will close and the updater will open. Don't reopen Hermes yourself; it restarts automatically when the update finishes. [hermes] [updates] state.db pre-flight: size=175353856, headerOk=true, ... [hermes] [updates] venv shim unlocked; safe to proceed [hermes] Hermes backend exited (1) [hermes] [boot] An update is finishing — Hermes will start automatically when it completes… [hermes] [updates] launched repo hand-off script: ...\scripts\desktop-update\windows.ps1 (branch main); exiting desktop to release venv shim [hermes] [updates] detached update finished with manual action (branch main): Update complete. Reopen Hermes to finish (it could not restart itself). ``` The same `Hermes backend exited (1)` line appears ~10 times across the two update events; the app does **not** restart itself after the update completes — the user has to manually close and reopen it every time. ### 2. `hermes update` fails: git install → ZIP fallback → both hit WinError 32 `update.log` (2026-08-14 16:41): ``` ⚠ hermes.exe is locked by another process; scheduled replacement on next reboot. error: failed to remove file `...\hermes-agent\venv\Lib\site-packages\../../Scripts/hermes.exe`: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32) ⚠ Git update failed: Command '[...\uv.exe', 'pip', 'install', '-e', '.']' returned non-zero exit status 2. → Falling back to ZIP download... ✗ ZIP update failed: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process: '...\hermes-agent\ui-tui' -> '...\hermes-agent\ui-tui.hermes-update-old' ``` Same pattern in `hermes-update.log` (2026-07-31): `hermes.exe` locked by another process (os error 32) → git update failed → ZIP fallback → `WinError 32` on `ui-tui` rename. ### 3. Secondary noise during boot `desktop.log`: ``` [hermes] [boot] could not read served dashboard token (Hermes backend): 404: {"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled — use `hermes dashboard` for the browser UI."} ⚠ Deprecated .env settings detected: TERMINAL_CWD=... (move to config.yaml terminal.cwd) ``` ## Expected behavior - `hermes update` / desktop self-update completes on Windows **without** WinError 32 lock failures (detect/kill the processes holding `hermes.exe` and `.pyd`/`ui-tui` files, or use a staged/reboot-safe replacement). - The desktop app restarts itself after the detached update finishes instead of requiring a manual reopen ("it could not restart itself"). - No `Hermes backend exited (1)` during the update hand-off window. ## Workaround used Close the desktop app fully, run the update, then manually reopen — works, but every update requires this manual dance and the ZIP fallback still leaves a partially-updated tree. ## Related - #63717 — Windows: Hermes Desktop update failures (comprehensive diagnostic, 7 correlated root causes) - #68760 — hermes.exe locked during `hermes update` on Windows (WinError 32)

signal.title: fix(plugins): register platform-plugin client tools during deferred discovery (#81163)
signal.text: ## Summary The bundled a2a-platform plugin's five outbound client tools (a2a_call, a2a_discover, a2a_list, a2a_history, a2a_orchestrate) never reach the agent's tool catalog, because they sit inside the plugin's register(ctx) — and register(ctx) itself never fires: PluginManager._register_deferred_platform defers every 'kind: platform' plugin to a lazy loader that only runs when the gateway / cron / setup / send_message path first asks the platform_registry for that platform. The inbound adapter stays deferred (heavy SDKs aren't pulled in for plain hermes chat), but the client-tool registration has no reason to be tied to it. This commit fixes both layers described in #81163. ## Fix ### Layer 1 — eager client-tool registration in the deferred path PluginManager._register_deferred_platform now additionally tries to import the plugin module and, if a top-level register_tools(ctx) callable exists, invokes it during discover_plugins(). The plugin's __init__.py is a thin re-export of register (matching the bundled-platform convention), so this import stays cheap — the heavy adapter module remains lazy. The eager call only runs the plugin's client/agent tools registration; the platform adapter's ctx.register_platform(...) is left for the deferred loader, avoiding a duplicate platform_registry.register(...). The a2a plugin opts into this entry point by exposing its existing tools.register_tools as a top-level symbol on the package. Other bundled platform plugins without client tools are unaffected (no register_tools attribute → no-op). ### Layer 2 — _get_platform_tools admits explicit plugin toolsets tools_config._get_platform_tools computed plugin_ts_keys = _get_plugin_toolset_keys() but only used CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS in the explicit-config filter. A user-listed key like a2a in 'platform_toolsets.cli: [hermes-cli, a2a]' was therefore silently dropped. The filter now unions configurable and plugin toolset keys when evaluating has_explicit_config and when admitting per-key entries, so explicitly-configured plugin toolsets survive. ## Verification ```python from hermes_cli.plugins import discover_plugins, get_plugin_toolsets from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_plugin_toolset_keys discover_plugins() sorted({k for k,_,_ in get_plugin_toolsets()}) # ['a2a', 'spotify'] sorted(_get_plugin_toolset_keys()) # ['a2a', 'spotify'] ``` a2a is now present (was absent before). End-to-end Layer 2 check: ```python from hermes_cli.tools_config import _get_platform_tools _get_platform_tools({'platform_toolsets': {'cli': ['hermes-cli', 'a2a']}}, 'cli') # 'a2a' is in the returned enabled-toolsets set ``` ## Tests - tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py::TestDeferredPlatformClientTools - test_eager_register_tools_runs_for_deferred_platform — registers a synthetic bundled platform plugin with a top-level register_tools and asserts (a) the placeholder is recorded deferred, (b) the adapter's register() did NOT run, (c) the client toolset appears in get_plugin_toolsets() immediately, (d) discover_plugins() is idempotent. Fails before the fix (Layer 1). - test_deferred_platform_without_register_tools_is_a_noop — bundled platform plugins without register_tools still register their deferred loader cleanly. - tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py - test_explicit_plugin_toolset_admitted_in_platform_toolsets — hermetic stub of _get_plugin_toolset_keys asserts an explicit plugin key alongside hermes-cli survives the _get_platform_tools filter (Layer 2). - test_explicit_plugin_toolset_admitted_against_real_a2a_plugin — end-to-end check: with the real bundled a2a plugin discoverable, a config like 'platform_toolsets.cli: [hermes-cli, a2a]' produces an enabled-toolsets set containing a2a. Fails before the fix (Layer 2). ## Test runs ``` python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py -q # 70 passed ``` `python -m ruff check hermes_cli/plugins.py hermes_cli/tools_config.py plugins/platforms/a2a/__init__.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins.py tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py` # All checks passed! Fixes #81163

signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a false-positive `hermes sessions recover --inspect-only` result when SQLite can answer `COUNT(*)` from a healthy covering index while canonical table payload pages are malformed. `inspect_session_database()` now performs a bounded-memory, full-column table scan with `NOT INDEXED`. Normal recovery keeps its lightweight pre-copy inventory because the copy phase already traverses every payload, avoiding a redundant full-database read. ## Related Issue Fixes #86224 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Add an opt-in payload scan to `hermes_cli/session_recovery.py` inspection internals. - Force inspection scans through the canonical table B-tree with `NOT INDEXED` and materialize one full row at a time. - Add `payload_readable` to deep per-table inspection results and preserve existing lightweight inventory behavior for normal recovery. - Add physical SQLite regressions for both directions: a malformed `messages` table leaf with a readable covering count index, and a malformed covering index with readable table payloads. ## How to Test 1. Run `HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/python scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery.py -q`. 2. Run `HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/python scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/hermes_cli -q`. 3. signal.title: sessions recover reports complete after omitting durable auxiliary state
signal.text: ## Bug Description On current `main` (`de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe`), `hermes sessions recover` can report all of the following: ```text complete: true verified: true verification.loss_detected: false verification.errors: [] verification.warnings: [] ``` while silently omitting durable state from the source database: 1. the entire lazy-created `delivery_obligations` table, including non-terminal owed replies; and 2. source-only columns added by lazy schema migration, demonstrated by a non-empty `async_delegations.origin_session_id` value. The dangerous outbox case is not that terminal `delivered` rows are necessarily required forever; it is that non-terminal obligations (`pending`, `attempting`, `failed` — everything outside the pruned `delivered`/`abandoned` set) can disappear without any recovery warning. The terminal-row retention policy can remain a maintainer decision. ## Steps to Reproduce This was reproduced with a synthetic fixture against the upstream commit above; no live user database or private message content is involved. 1. Create a fresh `SessionDB` with one session and one message. 2. Initialize the current delivery-ledger schema with `gateway.delivery_ledger._initialize_schema()`. 3. Initialize the current async-delegation lazy schema with `tools.async_delegation._initialize_schema()`. 4. Insert: - one `delivery_obligations` row in `pending` state; - one row in `delivered` state; - one `async_delegations` row whose `origin_session_id` is non-empty. 5. Run strict `recover_session_database(source, output)`. 6. Inspect the output schema and recovery report. Actual recovery-report fields: ```json { "complete": true, "verified": true, "verification": { "loss_detected": false, "errors": [], "warnings": [] } } ``` The synthetic harness separately observed that the source contained one `pending` and one `delivered` obligation, the destination had no `delivery_obligations` table, the source had `async_delegations.origin_session_id`, and the destination did not. These are harness observations, not keys emitted by `recover_session_database()`. The recovered `async_delegations` row exists, but its source-only `origin_session_id` column and value do not. ## Expected Behavior A recovery output must not be reported as complete and lossless when non-terminal durable delivery obligations or non-default source-only canonical columns were omitted. At minimum, the recovery report should: - inventory relevant auxiliary durable tables; - list omitted source tables and source-only columns; - detect whether omitted columns contain non-null/non-default values; - set `loss_detected: true` and `complete: false` when durable data was omitted; - warn explicitly about non-terminal delivery obligations that were not preserved. The eventual data-preservation policy can be handled separately: - whether to copy every obligation or only non-terminal rows; - whether recovered owner PID stamps should be cleared/reassigned; - whether lazy initializers should move into the base schema or be registered with recovery. ## Actual Behavior `recover_session_database()` initializes the destination only through base `SessionDB`, then copies a fixed canonical table list. `_copy_table()` selects only the intersection of destination and source columns: ```python source_columns = _table_columns(source, table) destination_columns = _table_columns(destination, table) columns = [column for column in destination_columns if column in source_columns] ``` The copy is marked `complete` when copied row count equals source row count, even if source-only columns with non-empty values were dropped. `delivery_obligations` is not inventoried or copied at all. The destination does not initialize that lazy table, and the report emits no omission warning. ## Affected Component CLI (`hermes sessions recover`) / session-state recovery / gateway durability ledger. ## Messaging Platform N/A for reproduction. The omitted obligations can belong to any gateway platform. ## Debug Report Not uploaded: this is a deterministic synthetic fixture on current upstream `main`. It contains only placeholder strings and no configuration, credentials, logs, platform identifiers, or user data. ## Operating System Linux 6.8.0-63-generic x86_64 ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version `main@de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe` (`v2026.8.13-106-gde0abc0617`) ## Root Cause Analysis There are two related completeness gaps: 1. **Fixed recovery inventory:** `delivery_obligations` is created lazily in `gateway/delivery_ledger.py` and is absent from the recovery table set. 2. **Schema intersection without loss accounting:** base `hermes_state_common.py` creates `async_delegations` without `origin_session_id`; `tools/async_delegation.py` adds it lazily. Recovery initializes only the base schema, copies common columns, compares row counts, and reports the table complete. This is separate from open PR #67078, which addresses live gateway crash/replay semantics rather than offline `state.db` recovery. Related but distinct: #86224 concerns `--inspect-only` failing to traverse malformed canonical payload pages. ## Proposed Fix First, make the report honest without prematurely deciding replay semantics: - record omitted tables and source-only columns; - inspect whether omitted data is materially populated; - classify populated omissions as loss; - report non-terminal delivery-obligation state counts and fail closed or warn prominently. Follow-up preservation work can then initialize current runtime schemas and copy/reconcile obligations under a maintainer-approved replay policy. ## PR willingness Focused reporting PR: #86245. The actual obligation-preservation policy remains a separate follow-up after maintainer confirmation.

signal.title: sessions recover --inspect-only can miss malformed canonical payload pages
signal.text: ## Bug Description On current `main` (`de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe`), `hermes sessions recover --inspect-only` can report `recoverable: true` when a required canonical table's payload B-tree is malformed. The inspection path treats `PRAGMA table_info(...)` plus `SELECT COUNT(*)` as proof that a table is completely readable. SQLite may satisfy `COUNT(*)` from a healthy covering index without touching damaged table payload pages. Strict recovery later selects the payload columns and fails. This makes `--inspect-only` a false health signal precisely in the corruption case it is intended to diagnose. ## Steps to Reproduce I reproduced this with a synthetic SQLite fixture against the upstream commit above; no user database or private content is involved. 1. Create one session with 320 messages whose payloads are 1,500 bytes each. 2. Checkpoint, switch to `journal_mode=DELETE`, and `VACUUM` so the `messages` table spans multiple leaves. 3. Confirm that SQLite plans `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM messages` through the covering index `idx_messages_session_id`. 4. Corrupt the two-byte cell-count field beginning at page-header offset 3 of one middle `messages` **table** leaf, while leaving `idx_messages_session_id` untouched. The synthetic fixture and exact corrupting edit are included in PR #86237. 5. Run `inspect_session_database(source)` (the implementation behind `--inspect-only`). 6. Run strict `recover_session_database(source, output)`. Observed fixture facts: ```text count query plan: SCAN messages USING COVERING INDEX idx_messages_session_id count result: 320 SELECT * FROM messages: database disk image is malformed inspect tables.messages.rows: 320 inspect recoverable: true strict messages copy status: failed strict messages copied_rows: 0 strict messages error: database disk image is malformed strict recovery complete: false strict recovery verified: false ``` ## Expected Behavior Inspection should traverse the canonical payload projection that strict recovery needs, using bounded memory. A malformed required-table payload should not produce `recoverable: true` merely because a secondary index can answer `COUNT(*)`. At minimum, the per-table inspection result should distinguish count/index readability from payload readability. Ideally the top-level report should also distinguish required-session salvageability from strict all-canonical-table recoverability. ## Actual Behavior `_table_inventory()` records a table as available and readable after: ```python columns = _table_columns(conn, table) result["rows"] = int( conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{table}"').fetchone()[0] ) ``` `_inspect_connection()` then declares the source recoverable when the `sessions` and `messages` counts are non-null. No payload row is read during inspection. ## Affected Component CLI (`hermes sessions recover --inspect-only`) / session-state recovery. ## Messaging Platform N/A (offline CLI recovery). ## Debug Report Not uploaded: this is a deterministic synthetic corruption fixture on current upstream `main`, with no live configuration, credentials, logs, session text, or user database. All relevant aggregate output is included above. ## Operating System Linux 6.8.0-63-generic x86_64 ## Python Version Python 3.11.15 ## Hermes Version `main@de0abc0617794a8c4ae661d2f67f4b23d4ab51fe` (`v2026.8.13-106-gde0abc0617`) ## Root Cause Analysis `hermes_cli/session_recovery.py::_table_inventory()` uses `SELECT COUNT(*)` as its only row-read probe. SQLite is free to answer that query from a covering index. Damage confined to table leaves or overflow pages is therefore not touched until `_copy_table()` executes `SELECT <all compatible columns> FROM <table>`. This is separate from: - #80205, which addressed `--allow-partial` rowid range-budget exhaustion; - #80255, which concerns the WAL `TRUNCATE` checkpoint shutdown corruption path; - #32687, which predates the current offline recovery command. Related but distinct: #86236 concerns silent omission of durable auxiliary state after source payloads are readable. ## Proposed Fix - Stream the canonical table's full column projection for `--inspect-only` rather than treating `COUNT(*)` as a payload-readability proof. - Use `NOT INDEXED` so a healthy secondary index cannot mask malformed payload pages, and so a damaged rebuildable secondary index does not create a false negative for table data. - Count rows during that streaming scan instead of materializing the table in memory. - Keep the normal recovery pre-copy inventory lightweight; strict recovery already reads every payload during copy, so it should not double-scan large databases. - Record payload-read errors explicitly in the per-table report. - Add a physical SQLite regression fixture that corrupts a table leaf while preserving the covering count index. ## PR willingness Focused regression PR: #86237.

signal.title: feat(telegram): honor config.yaml extra for inbound text batch delay
signal.text: ## Problem Telegram already batches inbound text, but short bubbles are hard-capped at **180ms / 240ms** (`_TEXT_BATCH_FAST_DELAY_S` / `_TEXT_BATCH_SHORT_DELAY_S`, PR #10388). Raising `HERMES_TELEGRAM_TEXT_BATCH_DELAY_SECONDS` cannot lift that cap (`min(configured, 0.18)`). Real users send context as several bubbles (file, then instruction, then a follow-up). The agent starts on the first fragment. WhatsApp already exposes `platforms.whatsapp.extra.text_batch_delay_seconds` and honors it. Telegram did not. ## Approach - Read `platforms.telegram.extra.text_batch_delay_seconds` / `text_batch_split_delay_seconds` / `media_batch_delay_seconds` (same keys as WhatsApp). - **When `text_batch_delay_seconds` extra is set**, skip the 180ms/240ms adaptive caps so the configured quiet period is the quiet period. - **When extra is unset**, keep the PR #10388 default (short replies still feel instant). No default-latency change. - Env vars remain a fallback and still do **not** lift the short-message caps (behavior stays in `config.yaml`, not `.env`). - Extract `_text_batch_quiet_seconds` so tests hit production logic. ## Tests - Existing adaptive-tier tests now call `_text_batch_quiet_seconds`. - New: extra set → 3s delay on a 20-char bubble; split-threshold still uses split delay; `_extra_has` reads `PlatformConfig.extra`. - Sabotage: disabling the extra branch makes the new test fail (`0.18 == 3.0`). - `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/gateway/test_telegram_text_batch_perf.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_text_batching.py` → 12 passed. ## Docs `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/telegram.md` — Message batching section, mirrored on WhatsApp. ## Risk - Defaults unchanged if extra is unset. - File-then-separate-text still use different queues (media vs text). Out of scope; caption-on-file remains the workaround for that mix. Closes nothing (no open issue for this exact gap; #2434 already shipped the original batcher).

signal.title: fix(desktop): local profile switch reuses default socket after update
signal.text: ## Summary After a recent Desktop update, selecting any local named profile from the profile rail can leave Desktop attached to the default profile. The named backend starts successfully, but Desktop never opens its persistent WebSocket and continues using the primary/default socket. This affects current `main` and makes local multi-profile switching appear inert: the profile is selectable, but the sidebar/active agent remains on the same profile. ## Environment - Hermes Desktop on macOS 26.6.1 (Apple silicon) - Local primary profile: `default` - Local named profile: `fiction-writer` - Reproduced from current `main` around `486f4ace20ba75401681c0915ab79a0968fa6bb1` - Confirmed still present after fetching current `origin/main` ## Reproduction 1. Configure Desktop with the local `default` profile and at least one local named profile. 2. Launch Desktop on `default`. 3. Select the named profile from the profile rail. 4. Observe that the named backend starts and passes the one-shot WebSocket probe. 5. Observe that no persistent WebSocket is opened for the named profile and the Desktop context remains attached to the primary/default socket. ## Expected behavior A local named profile should use its own pooled backend and persistent WebSocket. The sidebar, sessions, model, tools, and agent context should move to that profile. ## Actual behavior The local pooled descriptor is mistaken for a shared-primary descriptor. Desktop reuses the primary/default socket instead of dialing the named profile's pooled backend. Representative log sequence: ```text Starting Hermes backend for profile "fiction-writer" ... HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=64271 Hermes backend listening on 127.0.0.1:64271 ... tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted ... tui_gateway.ws: ws closed ... messages=0 ``` The accepted/closed connection is the startup probe. There is no subsequent persistent profile WebSocket. ## Root cause `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts::sharedPrimaryRoute()` currently treats the presence of `connection.profile` as proof that the descriptor uses the shared primary backend: ```ts return Boolean(conn && typeof conn === 'object' && (conn as { profile?: string }).profile) ``` However, `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts::spawnPoolBackend()` intentionally returns `profile` for local pooled descriptors as well. That profile value is needed so fresh WebSocket URL minting targets the correct backend. Therefore both of these descriptors carry `profile`: - a profile scoped onto the shared primary backend; - a dedicated local/remote pooled backend. The discriminator conflates those two routes. `ensureGatewayForProfile()` then takes the shared-primary branch for a local pool profile and never dials its socket. ## Proposed fix Add an explicit `sharedPrimary` marker only when `ensureBackend()` returns a profile-scoped primary descriptor, and make `sharedPrimaryRoute()` check that marker rather than inferring route ownership from `profile`. A regression test should assert both sides of the invariant: - `{ profile, sharedPrimary: true }` activates the primary socket; - a pooled descriptor carrying `{ profile }` still dials its own socket. ## Verification The proposed patch was tested locally: ```text Test Files 2 passed (2) Tests 13 passed (13) ``` Commands: ```bash cd apps/desktop npm test -- --run src/store/gateway-shared-remote.test.ts src/store/profile.test.ts npm run typecheck npm run pack ``` After installing the rebuilt package and restarting Desktop, switching between `default` and the local named profile works normally again.

signal.title: feat(buzz): add opt-in channel management tool
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Adds an opt-in `buzz_channels` tool for native Hermes Buzz gateway profiles. An approved agent can create a stream or forum channel and list channels visible to its active Buzz identity. This covers the agent-invoked part of [block/buzz#5758](https://github.com/block/buzz/issues/5758). It complements #82509 rather than replacing it: #82509 is operator-configured profile/channel synchronization, while this PR exposes a narrow model-facing create/list capability. The safety boundary is deliberate: - `buzz_admin` is off by default and must be enabled per Buzz profile with `hermes tools enable --platform buzz buzz_admin` - new channels default to private - the scoped Buzz private key travels through the child-process environment, never argv or tool output - the tool schema is unavailable unless the relay, scoped identity, and Buzz CLI are ready - update, archive, delete, and implicit file/content handling are not included ## Related Issue Related to [block/buzz#5758](https://github.com/block/buzz/issues/5758). ## Type of Change - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [x] 📝 Documentation update ## Changes Made - Added `plugins/platforms/buzz/channel_tools.py` with async create/list operations backed by the existing authenticated Buzz CLI seam. - Registered `buzz_admin` as a platform-restricted, default-off toolset. - Added Buzz to the canonical Hermes platform/toolset registry so profile-level enablement works. - Registered the tool through the bundled Buzz plugin and documented setup and safety limits. ## How to Test 1. Configure a native Buzz gateway profile with `BUZZ_RELAY_URL`, `BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY`, and the Buzz CLI. 2. Run `hermes tools enable --platform buzz buzz_admin`. 3. Ask Hermes to create a private channel, then list member channels and verify the returned ID, name, and description. Verified on macOS 26.5.1: - Real model-to-tool-to-Buzz CLI-to-relay round trip created a private channel, then found the exact ID, name, and description through `list`. - `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py tests/hermes_cli/test_skills_config.py tests/test_toolsets.py tests/gateway/test_buzz_adapter.py -q`: 96 passed, 0 failed. - Ruff check: passed. - Full suite: 31,594 passed, 15 failed, 331 skipped. The same 11 files produce the same 526 passed, 15 failed, 29 skipped on clean `origin/main` on this Mac. The failures are existing platform/environment assumptions, including Linux abstract sockets and WSL audio paths; this PR adds no failures. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the Contributing Guide - [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits - [x] I searched existing PRs and documented the boundary with #82509 - [x] My PR contains only related changes - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. See the identical `origin/main` macOS baseline above. - [ ] I've added tests for my changes. This feature uses the existing adapter and registry contracts; focused existing tests and a live relay round trip are reported above. - [x] I've tested on macOS 26.5.1 ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation - [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` is N/A; no config key was added - [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `AGENTS.md` are N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact; the implementation is stdlib plus the existing Buzz CLI adapter seam - [x] I've updated tool descriptions and schemas This is intentionally a building tool, not a “Burning Down the House” tool: destructive channel lifecycle operations remain operator actions.

signal.title: [Bug] Desktop: secondary profile's pooled serve is spawned but its WebSocket is never dialed — sidebar shows primary profile's project tree
signal.text: ## Summary Desktop app v0.20.1 (macOS, LOCAL mode, 2+ profiles): switching to a non-primary profile spawns that profile's pooled backend serve, but the renderer **never establishes a WebSocket connection to it**. The sidebar project tree therefore falls back to the last-known tree of the PRIMARY profile. Clicking any primary-profile project inside the secondary profile's view auto-switches the app back to the primary profile. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Have 2+ local profiles (primary + secondary) with distinct projects. 2. Open the app; the primary tree renders in the sidebar. 3. Switch to the secondary profile via the rail. 4. Observed: the sidebar STILL shows the primary profile's projects (project-tree grouping). The secondary profile's own projects never appear. 5. Click any primary-profile project → the app switches the active profile back to primary (pill changes) and opens the session. 6. Workaround found: switching sidebar grouping to **"updated"** (recent) shows the secondary profile's sessions correctly — that list path IS profile-scoped. So session data routing is fine; only the project tree is wrong. ## Evidence - Fresh app restart, 3 serves spawned at boot: - primary serve: holds the app's ESTABLISHED connections (2). - secondary serve: spawned as `--profile <secondary> serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0`, LISTENING on its ephemeral port, but **0 ESTABLISHED connections** from the app (`lsof -nP -a -p <pid> -iTCP`). - External WS probe of the secondary serve + `projects.tree` returns the CORRECT tree (its own projects only). The backend is healthy; the renderer just never dials it. - Persists across full app restarts (Cmd+Q), not just a reload. Not the all-profiles browse mode (`hermes.desktop.showAllProfiles` = false in localStorage). ## Expected behavior Switching to a profile shows that profile's own project tree in the sidebar. ## Environment - macOS 15.7.5 (arm64), Hermes Desktop v0.20.1 - Local profiles only, no remote gateway / no per-profile connection overrides ## Code trail (source at current HEAD) - `apps/desktop/src/store/profile.ts` — `selectProfile()` → `ensureGatewayProfile(name)` - `apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts` — `ensureGatewayForProfile()` → `openSecondary()` → `desktop.getConnection(profile)` → `entry.gateway.connect(wsUrl)`; on failure `scheduleReconnect(entry)` runs and `setActive(key)` STILL executes, so `$activeGatewayProfile` moves to the secondary profile while its socket is dead. - `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — `ensureBackend()` returns the pooled `connectionPromise`; `spawnPoolBackend()` self-probes `/api/ws` before declaring ready, so the descriptor looks valid. - `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` — `refreshProjectTree()` → `activeProjectsContext()` → `activeGateway()`; with a dead secondary gateway the refresh fails and the cached (primary) tree is kept by design ("failure leaves the cached tree intact so the sidebar doesn't flicker"). ## Possibly related - #77005 (remote mode, same symptom family: sidebar shows launch profile's projects) - #75308 (projects_db_path per-profile) - #74551 (wrong profile backend after reconnect)

signal.title: skill_view fails when skill front matter contains an unquoted YAML date
signal.text: ## Bug: `skill_view` fails on unquoted YAML dates in skill front matter ### Summary Hermes can discover a local skill, but `skill_view` fails when the skill's YAML front matter contains an unquoted ISO date such as: ```yaml updated: 2026-03-05 ``` The YAML parser resolves this value to a Python `date` object. Hermes then attempts to return the skill metadata as JSON and errors because that object is not JSON serializable. ### Observed error ``` {"error": "Object of type date is not JSON serializable", "success": false} ``` ### Environment - Hermes Agent: v0.20.0 - Commit: `b3aa561faffd64f05436e429a6415d175e534ec9` - Python: 3.11.15 - OS: Linux - Skill source: `alirezarezvani/claude-skills`, `ceo-advisor` ### Reproduction 1. Install or place a skill containing: ```yaml --- name: dated-skill description: Example updated: 2026-03-05 --- ``` 2. Run Hermes with that skill available. 3. Call `skill_view("dated-skill")`. Expected: Hermes returns the skill content and metadata. Actual: Hermes returns the JSON serialization error above. Skill listing still works; the failure occurs when loading the full skill view. ### Possible direction Normalize YAML-native `date`/`datetime` values to ISO strings before returning JSON, or otherwise make the skill response serializer handle those scalar types. This would preserve valid YAML metadata without requiring every skill author to quote dates. I am reporting this rather than proposing a repository patch so the maintainers can choose the best implementation.

signal.title: fix(cli): report omitted session recovery state
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Makes offline session-recovery reports account for durable source state that the current recovery contract does not copy. This PR is deliberately reporting-only. It does **not** copy or replay delivery obligations, change ownership fields, or initialize plugin/gateway schemas in the destination. Those behaviors need a separate maintainer-approved recovery policy because replaying already delivered work can duplicate user-visible messages. ## Related Issue Addresses the reporting portion of #86236. It intentionally leaves replay, retention, and schema-ownership policy open for maintainer discussion. ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - Inventory omitted `delivery_obligations` rows by state without copying or re-owning them. - Treat `pending`, `attempting`, `failed`, unknown, and NULL states as non-terminal; mark the recovery lossy when any such obligations are omitted. - Report omitted terminal obligations without declaring them data loss, preserving the current anti-duplicate-delivery policy boundary. - Compare source and destination schemas for copied tables, list source-only columns, and detect values that differ from declared literal defaults or known application-level empty sentinels (`NULL` / `''` for `origin_session_id`). - Cross-check `sqlite_master` so `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON` cannot silently hide a malformed source table schema from omission reporting. - Propagate material omissions into `verification.loss_detected`, `partial`, and `complete` while leaving structural `verified` semantics unchanged. - Add a distinct CLI result for structurally verified output with known omissions: exit 0, keep `complete: false`, print the omission warnings, and require report review before installation instead of claiming verification failed. - Keep the report shape additive in page-level lost-and-found mode by marking omission inventory as unavailable rather than omitting the section. - Add synthetic tests for lossy non-terminal/lazy-column state, terminal-only state with both semantic empty sentinels, malformed auxiliary schema, a source-only literal-default column, lost-and-found report shape, and both CLI exit/message paths. ## How to Test 1. Run `HERMES_PYTHON=/path/to/python scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery.py tests/hermes_cli/test_session_recovery_lost_and_found.py -q`. 2. No user database, credentials, internal address, platform token, or session content is included. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux 6.8.0-63-generic, Python 3.11.14 (uv standalone runtime) The full repository and complete `tests/hermes_cli` suites were not run on this branch. signal.title: fix(gateway): stop internal bookkeeping writes from advancing the session activity clock
signal.text: ## Summary Background bookkeeping writes no longer advance a session's user-activity clock, so a long-idle session can't be falsely marked `resume_pending` after a gateway restart. `updated_at` is the single activity clock driving idle/daily reset policy and the restart-resume freshness gate (`suspend_recently_active`, #85709). Two internal stamp sites remained after 784f733cf (recover derives `updated_at` from the durable row) and 5462f689b (`touch_activity` gating): `set_session_metadata()` (e.g. Slack thread watermarks) and `advance_compression_session()`'s repoint both stamped `updated_at = now` on writes that carry no user activity. ## Changes - `gateway/session.py`: drop the `updated_at` stamp in `set_session_metadata()` and `advance_compression_session()`; durable saves unchanged. - `tests/gateway/test_session.py`, `tests/gateway/test_session_store_runtime_stale_guard.py`: regression tests asserting a 21-day-idle session stays invisible to `suspend_recently_active()` after each write. Both fail on the old behavior (sabotage-verified). ## Validation | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | metadata write on 21d-idle session, then restart gate | marked `resume_pending` | count 0 | | compression repoint on 21d-idle session, then restart gate | marked `resume_pending` | count 0 | | targeted suite (test_session, runtime_stale_guard, clean_shutdown_marker) | — | 78/78 pass | Follow-up to #85895 (closed) — credit to @GodsBoy for pushing on this bug class and @chelsealong for the #85709 analysis. ## Infographic ![Session clock integrity infographic](https://files.catbox.moe/2f9u6f.png)

signal.title: Desktop: sameCronSignature drops pin/archive-only session updates
signal.text: ## Bug On current `main`, Desktop session refreshes discard pages whose only changes are row-state flags. `sameCronSignature()` in `apps/desktop/src/lib/session-signatures.ts` compares content and recency fields, but not `pinned` or `archived`. `refreshSessions()` therefore keeps the previous atom when a fetched page changes only one of those flags: ```ts return sameCronSignature(prev, next) ? prev : next ``` The backend write succeeds, but `$sessions` can retain the stale row indefinitely for an idle conversation. For pinning, that stale row is then consumed by `session-pin-sync`; once its confirmation guard expires, an old `pinned: true` row can resurrect an item the user already unpinned. The same omission makes archive-only changes invisible to this signature gate. ## Distinct from earlier pin races This is not the earlier pull-before-push race fixed by #75973 for #74570. It is also one layer above the write-confirmation guard added by #77170 for #76919: the guard has a valid confirmation path, but the page carrying the confirming `pinned` value is filtered out before it can reach the reconciler. ## Reproduction 1. Start with an idle pinned conversation, so no title, preview, count, or timestamp field is moving. 2. Unpin it and confirm the backend row changes to `pinned = 0`. 3. Let session refresh return the same row with only `pinned` changed. 4. The page is judged signature-equal and discarded; the cached row remains `pinned: true`. After the write guard expires, a later reconciliation can re-adopt that stale value. A focused unit test that changes only `pinned` fails on current `main`; the equivalent archive-only test fails as well. ## Expected behavior `sameCronSignature()` should treat both `pinned` and `archived` as significant row state, with regression tests for pin-only and archive-only deltas. This causes one atom update per deliberate pin or archive action and does not reintroduce ordinary session-page churn. ## Proposed fix PR #86218 implements the minimal fix and regression coverage: - compare `session.pinned === other.pinned` - compare `session.archived === other.archived` - add pin-only, archive-only, and unchanged-state tests No additional `session-pin-sync` retry behavior is required for this issue unless a fresh reproduction remains after the confirming page is allowed through.
signal.author: james47kjv

signal.title: Relay-fronted cron delivery: out-of-process runs have no transport (relay registers no standalone_sender_fn) — scheduled reports never reach Discord on Hermes Cloud
signal.text: Scheduled cron jobs on a relay-fronted deployment (Hermes Cloud instance behind the Team Gateway connector) execute fine but never deliver: every run ends with `platform 'discord' not configured/enabled`. The in-process path for this exact topology works and is tested; the gap is that Chronos-triggered cron runs execute out-of-process, and the relay platform registers no `standalone_sender_fn`, so out-of-process delivery has no transport at all. ## Environment - Hermes Cloud instance (always-on), relay-only: `config.yaml` `platforms:` contains only the `relay` block, no native `discord` credentials (by design — the connector holds the bot token). - Interactive traffic works perfectly: inbound DMs and replies ride the live gateway's relay websocket. - Cron jobs created from the Discord DM session with `deliver=origin` (`origin.platform=discord`). ## Symptom Every scheduled run: agent executes, report is written to disk, then ``` WARNING cron.scheduler: Job 'c588c14f3abf': platform 'discord' not configured/enabled ``` `last_status: ok`, `last_delivery_error: platform 'discord' not configured/enabled`. Same for `hermes cron run <id>` from a shell. Execution records show `source=chronos` — the runs are triggered out-of-process relative to the live gateway. ## Diagnosis (source at head) 1. Out-of-process delivery resolves through the standalone path, which requires the platform's `PlatformEntry.standalone_sender_fn` (`tools/send_message_tool.py:747`, error string at `:778`). 2. Discord's native plugin registers one (`plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:10147`) — but a relay-only deployment has no native Discord config, so the logical-platform lookup fails first. 3. The relay platform's own `PlatformEntry` registers **no** `standalone_sender_fn` (`gateway/relay/__init__.py:955-965` — `adapter_factory`, `check_fn`, no standalone hook). Probing `deliver=relay:<chat_id>` directly confirms: ``` delivery error: No live adapter for platform 'relay'. Is the gateway running with this platform connected? For out-of-process delivery (e.g. cron in a separate process), the platform plugin must register a standalone_sender_fn on its PlatformEntry. ``` 4. The **in-process** path handles this topology correctly and is pinned by tests: `tests/cron/test_relay_fronted_delivery.py::TestRelayDeliveryGate::test_relay_fronted_platform_is_not_rejected` ("a live relay transport that fronts Discord must deliver even though platforms.discord has no native config block at all"), plus the preflight guard in `tests/cron/test_cron_relay_delivery_guards.py`. So fire-time routing via `resolve_delivery_transport` + `fronts_platform` is all there — it just never runs, because on Hermes Cloud the scheduler executing the job is not the gateway process. Net effect: on a relay-only hosted instance, every out-of-process cron delivery target except `local` fails identically, while the same job's delivery would succeed if executed inside the gateway process. ## Fix options (design call, hence issue not PR) 1. **`standalone_sender_fn` for the relay platform**: dial the connector, handshake, send one egress frame, close. Caveat that makes this non-obvious: the connector treats a new handshake as a resume trigger (`gateway/relay/__init__.py` transport comment: re-handshake triggers the buffered-flip drain), and the live gateway already holds a socket for the same gateway identity — a second concurrent socket may disrupt it. If the connector multiplexes per-connection rather than per-gateway-id this is safe; that's connector-semantics knowledge a maintainer has and I don't. 2. **Loopback IPC to the live gateway**: the standalone sender POSTs to the local gateway's API server and the live process sends via its existing relay socket. No second socket, no handshake question; adds an API-server route (or reuses one if a send route already exists). 3. **Chronos-side**: for always-on instances, have the Chronos trigger hand execution to the gateway process (in-process scheduler), where delivery already works. Scale-to-zero instances still need (1) or (2) for the wake-up case. Happy to build whichever direction is preferred — (2) looks safest from outside, but the connector team knows whether (1)'s second socket is harmless. ## Repro Any relay-only deployment: create a cron job with `deliver=origin` from a Discord session fronted by the connector, let it fire, read `last_delivery_error`.

signal.title: fix(agent): reject system-role injection from context-engine selection
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Fixes a security-hardening gap where `_apply_context_engine_selection` accepted any non-empty list of dicts returned by a `ContextEngine.select_context()` extension and shipped it verbatim. A malicious or buggy engine could therefore inject an attacker-controlled `system` message (a policy override) or replace the host's protected system prompt — and the downstream `_sanitize_api_messages` pass does not strip system-role messages. This PR validates the replacement before returning it: - the leading `system` messages must match the original protected prefix verbatim (role + content); - no additional `system`-role message may appear beyond that prefix; - every message must carry a valid role, and `tool` messages must have a `tool_call_id`. Any violation fails open to the original request — legitimate reordering/filtering of *conversation* messages is still allowed. ## Related Issue Part of the SECURITY-AUDIT-42 hardening campaign (EPIC #82591), class `SECURITY-CLASS-963645940f301b6e`, consensus contract `R1-C-004`. Fixes #84262 ## Type of Change - [x] 🔒 Security fix ## Changes Made - `agent/conversation_loop.py` — added `_context_engine_selection_is_safe()` and wired it into `_apply_context_engine_selection` so a `select_context()` replacement is validated against the protected system prefix and role/tool-field contract before being returned. - `tests/agent/test_context_engine_select_context.py` — added four regression tests (system-role injection, prefix replacement, stray system message, tool message missing `tool_call_id`) plus one positive test for a valid filtered replacement. ## How to Test 1. `uv run python -m pytest tests/agent/test_context_engine_select_context.py -q` → 11 passed. 2. The four injection/tool-field tests fail on `origin/main` (the injected list was returned verbatim) and pass on this branch — proving the exact system-role injection this PR removes. 3. `uv run python -m pytest tests/agent/test_context_engine.py tests/agent/test_context_engine_host_contract.py tests/agent/test_engine_preflight_wire.py -q` → 21 passed. ## Checklist ### Code - [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) - [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate - [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits) - [x] I've run `pytest tests/agent/test_context_engine_select_context.py -q` and all tests pass - [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features) - [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15 (arm64) ### Documentation & Housekeeping - [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A - [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A - [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A - [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A

signal.title: fix(gateway): suppress duplicate final send after queued-followup fallback (#81052)
signal.text: Fixes #81052 When the queued-follow-up path fell back to calling `adapter.send()` on `first_response` (because streaming confirmation had not arrived in time), the normal completion pipeline that runs after the fallback was unaware the response had already been delivered. The user saw the same reply twice in their Slack DM / Discord channel / etc. Introduce `GatewayStreamConsumer.mark_out_of_band_delivery(text)` so the gateway can record a non-streaming delivery in a way the existing `_stream_confirmed_final_delivery` predicate recognises: it sets the same `final_response_sent` / `final_content_delivered` flags and records the payload via `_record_turn_final_payload` so `delivered_final_matches` reconciles cleanly with the completed `final_response`. `gateway/run.py` calls `_sc.mark_out_of_band_delivery(first_response)` immediately after the fallback `adapter.send()` returns. Subsequent normal-completion `_stream_confirmed_final_delivery(...)` returns `True` and the second send is suppressed. New tests in `tests/gateway/test_81052_queued_followup_double_send.py` lock in the flag set, the `delivered_final_matches` reconciliation (both `True` for matching text and `False` for stale payloads, mirroring #71643), and the empty-text no-op guard.

signal.title: fix(acp): pump stdio when stdout is not pipe-backed (#84515)
signal.text: Fixes #84515 ## Root cause The third-party ACP SDK (`acp/stdio.py`) calls `loop.connect_write_pipe(..., sys.stdout)` unconditionally. When a host app redirects or wraps stdout (regular file, etc.), that raises `ValueError: Pipe transport is only for pipes, sockets and character devices` at startup — breaking ACP integration with hosts like Open Design (0.19.0). ## Fix (hermes layer, SDK untouched) When stdout is not pipe-like, `acp_adapter/entry.py` now builds fallback stdio streams over the real stdio: - A daemon thread feeds `sys.stdin` line-by-line into an `asyncio.StreamReader`. - A custom `_StdoutWriteTransport` + `_DrainHelperProtocol` forward `StreamWriter` writes to `sys.stdout.buffer` (with working `drain()`). - `main()` logs a clear stderr warning (with fd modes) and runs `acp.run_agent(..., input_stream=writer, output_stream=reader, use_unstable_protocol=True)`. - Pipe-like stdio keeps the default SDK path byte-for-byte; Windows keeps its already-safe SDK behavior. ## Tests - `tests/acp/test_stdio_fallback.py`: 9 new tests — pipe-like detection (regular file / in-memory wrapper / real pipe), win32-vs-posix decision, pump round-trip over non-pipe stdio, `main()` routing with redirected stdout, and a full-protocol `initialize` round-trip through the real SDK `run_agent` over the pump. - `pytest tests/acp/ -q`: 134 passed, 1 failed — the failure is pre-existing and unrelated (Windows-Proactor pipe-cleanup ResourceWarning in `test_ping_suppression.py`; fails identically with changes stashed). - ruff clean on both changed files.

signal.title: fix(accounting): forward resolved api_key to /models metadata probe (#75479)
signal.text: Fixes #75479 The pricing/accounting code path in ``estimate_usage_cost`` reaches ``fetch_endpoint_model_metadata``, which probes a provider's ``/models`` and ``/v1/models`` endpoints for pricing metadata. When the provider gates ``/models`` behind authentication (LiteLLM proxy and similar), the probe must send an ``Authorization: Bearer`` header — but the resolved api_key never reached it because the auxiliary-client caller dropped the parameter on the floor: ```python record_aux_usage(response, task, provider=provider, base_url=base_url) _validate_llm_response(response, task, provider=..., base_url=...) _estimate_cost(model, ..., provider=..., base_url=...) ``` ## Fix Thread the ``api_key`` kwarg through all three call paths. - ``record_aux_usage()`` now accepts ``api_key`` and forwards it to ``estimate_usage_cost()``. Default is ``None`` — not ``""`` — so callers without a resolved key still work and we don't pretend a key is configured. - ``_validate_llm_response()`` now accepts ``api_key`` and forwards it through ``record_aux_usage()``. One call site in ``_async_call_llm_impl()`` that already had ``resolved_api_key`` in scope now passes it. - ``_estimate_cost()`` in ``agent/insights.py`` now accepts ``api_key`` for the same forward — live-creds callers (e.g. an authenticated insights query) can now use it. ## Regression tests The new ``TestAuxApiKeyForwarding`` and ``TestInsightsApiKeyForwarding`` classes cover: - ``record_aux_usage`` forwards ``api_key`` to ``estimate_usage_cost`` verbatim - Omitted ``api_key`` defaults to ``None`` (not the old silent ``""``) - ``_validate_llm_response`` accepts and forwards ``api_key`` - Static signature checks: both functions expose ``api_key`` as a keyword param - ``_estimate_cost`` forwards ``api_key`` to ``estimate_usage_cost`` - ``_estimate_cost`` omitted ``api_key`` defaults to ``None`` All 63 tests pass across the related modules (16 accounting + insights-related + usage_pricing). The spy patches the lazy import location (``agent.usage_pricing``) so the call from the function under test is observable. ## Files changed - ``agent/aux_accounting.py``: ``record_aux_usage()`` signature accepts ``api_key``, forwards to ``estimate_usage_cost`` - ``agent/auxiliary_client.py``: ``_validate_llm_response()`` signature accepts ``api_key``, forwards; ``_async_call_llm_impl()`` passes ``resolved_api_key`` - ``agent/insights.py``: ``_estimate_cost()`` signature accepts ``api_key``, forwards - ``tests/hermes_state/test_aux_usage_accounting.py``: 6 new tests across two classes

signal.title: fix: reset SSL ciphers to DEFAULT for WeChat CDN handshake (#84394)
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? WeChat's CDN (novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com) rejects Python's default restrictive cipher list with SSLV3_ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE, causing all media file downloads (documents, images) to fail. Text messages work fine because they don't hit the CDN. The root cause is in gateway/platforms/weixin.py::_make_ssl_connector(). It creates an ssl.create_default_context() but never resets the cipher list. Python's default context negotiates a restrictive set of ciphers that WeChat's CDN doesn't support. curl and other tools use OpenSSL's DEFAULT cipher list and connect fine. The fix adds ssl_ctx.set_ciphers("DEFAULT") after creating the context. This resets to OpenSSL's default cipher list (the same one curl uses) without weakening certificate verification — the CA bundle from certifi is still used for verification. The try/except guards against environments where the DEFAULT alias isn't available. The issue reporter verified this exact fix works: after adding set_ciphers("DEFAULT"), aiohttp connects to novac2c.cdn.weixin.qq.com successfully. ## Related Issue Fixes #84394 ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Testing - Added TestWeixinSSLCipherFix::test_ssl_connector_sets_default_ciphers regression test that verifies the SSL context has ciphers available after set_ciphers("DEFAULT") is called. - All 31 existing weixin tests still pass.

signal.title: feat(gateway): publish native remote turn activity
signal.text: ## What does this PR do? Publishes structured remote turn activity from the Hermes Gateway to Buzz so users can distinguish an actively working agent from a stalled or completed turn. The Gateway emits a neutral `TurnLifecycleEvent` contract for turn start, session resolution, progress, tool execution, completion, failure, and interruption. Buzz translates those events into allowlisted, owner-encrypted NIP-44 v2 observer frames without coupling Gateway core logic to Buzz wire semantics. Terminal outcomes are latched at the agent-execution boundary, before later delivery, TTS, cache-refresh, or queued-follow-up work can rewrite the result. Buzz retains terminal frames until positive relay acknowledgement, performs one bounded delayed same-generation retry after rejection or send failure, and preserves exhausted terminals for replay after the next authenticated WebSocket generation. The transport remains fail-open for Gateway execution and fail-safe for the Buzz UI: Activity requires WebSocket transport, polling fallback does not publish a false started state, stale-generation frames are not sent, retry cannot hot-loop, and cancellation during reset cannot leave `disconnect()` hanging while the WebSocket loop reconnects. Activity payloads are privacy allowlisted. They exclude prompts, tool arguments, tool outputs, credentials, and model response content. Tool identifiers are bounded and opaque, and internal retry metadata is removed before encryption. ## Related Issue Fixes #76678 Related Buzz consumer/relay tracking: https://github.com/block/buzz/issues/4964 ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] 🔒 Security fix - [ ] 📝 Documentation update - [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made - `gateway/turn_observer.py` - Adds the neutral `GatewayTurnObserver` and closed lifecycle-event contract. - Latches terminal outcomes and emits privacy-safe, bounded tool metadata. - `gateway/run.py` - Wraps normal, proxy, early-failure, and follow-up execution paths with the observer. - Preserves existing tool callbacks while adding structured lifecycle callbacks. - `gateway/platforms/base.py` - Adds the platform-neutral lifecycle adapter hook. - `plugins/platforms/buzz/adapter.py` - Translates lifecycle events into Buzz Activity frames. - Publishes signed, NIP-44-encrypted observer events over the authenticated WebSocket. - Correlates relay acknowledgements and retains terminal frames until positive acknowledgement. - Adds bounded delayed retry for negative relay acknowledgements and same-socket send failures. - Replays retained terminals after reconnect without stale-generation delivery or hot retry loops. - Uses cooperative sender shutdown while propagating cancellation so Gateway teardown cannot hang. - `plugins/platforms/buzz/nostr_auth.py` - Adds NIP-44 v2 encryption and observer-event construction. - `tests/gateway/test_turn_observer.py` - Covers lifecycle ordering, outcome latching, interruption/failure handling, privacy, and tool identifier bounds. - `tests/gateway/test_buzz_activity_bridge.py` - Covers Gateway-to-platform lifecycle translation, proxy/early-failure paths, callback preservation, and transport fallback behavior. - `tests/gateway/test_buzz_websocket.py` - Covers encrypted Activity publication, official NIP-44 vectors, acknowledgement retention, bounded retries, queue/reset behavior, cancellation propagation, and production-shaped disconnect/reconnect replay. - `website/docs/integrations/buzz.md` - Links the native Activity configuration and behavior documentation. - `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/buzz.md` - Documents `activity_owner_pubkey`, WebSocket requirements, encryption, retry/reconnect behavior, and terminal deduplication expectations. ## How to Test 1. Configure Buzz with authenticated WebSocket transport and an `activity_owner_pubkey`, start the Gateway, and send a turn that invokes a tool. Confirm Buzz receives ordered started, progress/tool, and terminal Activity frames without prompt, argument, output, or credential content. 2. Reject a terminal event with `['OK', event_id, false, 'rate-limited: slow down']`, and separately fail the first terminal WebSocket send while keeping the socket live. signal.title: fix(compression): require todo revalidation after compaction
signal.text: ## Summary Fixes #84718. Compaction is a provenance boundary: the conversation evidence, user framing, and skill policy that justified an active plan may have been summarized or pruned. Previously, however, active todo items crossed that boundary as executable `pending` / `in_progress` state. This allowed stale work to continue as though its original authorization and evidence were still present. This change preserves the useful plan, but invalidates its authority. Active items become `needs_reconfirmation`, evidence-gathering remains available, and action-capable tools remain blocked until the model explicitly revalidates, cancels, or completes the preserved items. ## Root cause The bug was not just missing reminder text. Three independent state paths treated stale plan state as current authority: 1. `TodoStore` had no non-actionable status for loss of provenance. 2. Post-compaction todo state only lived in synthetic prompt prose; a fresh agent could hydrate an older canonical tool result and resurrect actionable statuses. 3. Nothing enforced the reminder at dispatch time, so an action-capable tool could run without any todo transition. A prompt-only solution therefore cannot close the bug class. ## Competing PR comparison PR #84808 addresses the related skill-policy side by preserving a bounded textual rationale and asking the model to reload pruned skills. That is useful and complementary, but its preserved todo remains actionable and its safety property is advisory. This PR handles the plan-authorization side as a state-machine and dispatch invariant: - active work crosses compaction as non-actionable state; - the state is durable across restart/resume; - read-only evidence and skill inspection remain available; - action-capable tools are blocked until explicit revalidation. This is stronger for stale-plan continuation because correctness does not depend solely on the model following newly injected prose. It does not replace #84808's richer skill-provenance context; the two changes protect different halves of the same compaction boundary. ## Implementation ### State transition and atomicity - Add server-managed `needs_reconfirmation` state. - Transform only `pending` / `in_progress`; preserve terminal states. - Build the downgraded snapshot without mutating live state early. - Publish transcript and durable todo state at the same compression commit boundary. - Restore the prior in-memory plan if child publication fails. - Preserve strict message-role alternation and a byte-stable system prompt. ### Durable hydration - Persist bounded todo state in the session's private `model_config` metadata. - Update it whenever the todo store changes. - Prefer trusted session state over caller-supplied or stale transcript history. - Preserve authoritative empty state, preventing an older tool result from resurrecting cleared work. - Hydrate resumed gateway turns even when no transcript rows are supplied. - Preserve private model metadata during ACP saves using transactional config patching. - Keep the persistence callback attached across CLI `/new`, `/resume`, and branch transitions. ### Hard execution barrier - While any item needs reconfirmation, block action-capable tools centrally in the common dispatch path. - Keep `todo`, clarification, skills, file/search/session lookup, vision, and web evidence tools available. - Apply the barrier through sequential, concurrent, segmented, and tool-search dispatch because all paths converge on the guarded invocation. - A read-only todo call does not unlock execution; the state must actually transition. ### Client compatibility - Desktop and TUI parse, display, count, and retain `needs_reconfirmation` as unresolved work. - ACP maps the internal state to its closest portable pending plan status while labeling it as requiring reconfirmation. - The public wire format keeps the original `pending` enum plus an additive `needs_reconfirmation: true` flag. Independently upgraded older Desktop/TUI clients therefore retain the row instead of silently dropping an unknown enum; updated clients promote the flag to the internal state. ### Prompt/token cost The original per-item revalidation paragraph was replaced with one list-level instruction. With the maximum 256-item plan used in the regression benchmark: - original implementation: 48,338 characters; - revised implementation: 9,449 characters; - reduction: 38,889 characters (80.5%). Bounds remain enforced before persistence or injection. ## Tests Post-rebase verification against current `origin/main`: - Canonical Python wrapper over todo, compression success/failure, ACP event/persistence, turn hydration, and CLI new/resume/branch paths: - 9 files, 98 tests passed. - Focused run-agent hydration and dispatch barrier tests: - 8 tests passed. - Desktop Vitest: - 2 files, 17 tests passed. - TUI Vitest: - 2 files, 11 tests passed. - Desktop and TUI TypeScript typechecks passed. - Ruff passed for all changed Python files. - `git diff --check` passed. - Independent pre-commit review: PASS, no blocking logic or security findings. ## Risk and compatibility - No dependency or user configuration change. - The new status is internal/server-managed; model-authored todo inputs retain the existing public statuses. - Existing terminal statuses remain unchanged. - Metadata is bounded by existing todo item/content limits. - Session metadata writes occur only on todo changes, not every turn; hydration avoids redundant rewrites. - Caller-supplied legacy transcript history can hydrate the current turn but is not promoted into trusted durable session metadata. - The ACP metadata change replaces a race-prone read/replace pattern with an in-transaction patch, preserving unrelated private state. ## Checklist - [x] Reproduced and traced the stale-plan lifecycle. - [x] Compared the competing implementation and identified complementary scope. - [x] Fixed state semantics rather than adding prompt text alone. - [x] Added durable restart/resume coverage. - [x] Added dispatch-level enforcement and concurrent-path review. - [x] Covered ACP, Desktop, TUI, CLI session transitions, and failed publication rollback. - [x] Preserved prompt-cache and role-alternation invariants. - [x] Rebased onto current `origin/main` and reran focused validation.

signal.title: fix(desktop): stop adopting session providers without credentials into the composer
signal.text: ## Problem A session created under a provider whose credentials were later removed (OAuth revoked, API key deleted — e.g. switching away from xAI Grok OAuth) keeps stamping the dead provider on every `session.info` heartbeat. When the desktop app resumes such a session — including the **first-launch auto-restore of the most recent session** — `syncRuntimeMetadataToView` / `publishRuntimeToComposer` copy that provider into the **sticky composer state** (which is deliberately meant to be user UI state, not session-derivable). Every subsequent send then fails with a cryptic auth error: > No xAI OAuth credentials stored. Select xAI Grok OAuth (SuperGrok / Premium+) in `hermes model`. The desktop does not even classify this as a provider-setup error, so the user gets a raw error toast, the composer keeps the dead provider, and every retry fails the same way — with no recovery affordance. ### Repro 1. Use xAI Grok OAuth (or any provider), create a session. 2. Remove that provider's credentials (switch providers, revoke OAuth, delete the key). 3. Open the desktop app fresh — it auto-restores the most recent session. 4. Type a message → `No xAI OAuth credentials stored...`; every retry fails identically. ## Fix Three small desktop-side changes: 1. **Guard adoption of dead providers** — new `sessionProviderAdoptable()` in `lib/model-options.ts`, applied at the two composer-sync sites (`use-session-state-cache.ts`, `use-session-actions/utils.ts`). A session's provider is only mirrored into the sticky composer state when a **loaded** model-options catalog proves it still has credentials. The chat catalog is fetched `explicitOnly`, so an absent provider, or a row carrying `authenticated: false` (the re-auth skeleton the backend emits for the current provider), is not adopted. An unknown/not-yet-loaded catalog conservatively allows the sync — same philosophy as `manualPickRemoved` — so a still-valid pick is never clobbered by a stale catalog. `requestModelOptions` mirrors the last loaded provider list module-level so the sync paths (which run outside React) can read it synchronously. 2. **Recognize the error family** — `lib/provider-setup-errors.ts` now classifies `No ... credentials stored` (xAI OAuth, Codex, and future OAuth providers) as a provider-setup error, so the desktop routes it to the onboarding/setup affordance instead of a raw toast. 3. **Self-heal on failure** — in the gateway error handler (`use-message-stream/gateway-event.ts`), when a provider-setup error hits the active session while the composer holds an unauthenticated provider, reset the composer to the profile default so the next send succeeds instead of retry-looping. ## Tests - `sessionProviderAdoptable`: present/absent/`authenticated: false`/name-match/not-yet-loaded/empty-catalog cases, plus the cache-mirror variant. - `isProviderSetupErrorMessage`: new OAuth "credentials stored" cases, with the existing negative cases (env-var mentions, auxiliary warnings, runtime failures) preserved. - Existing suites for the touched modules pass (`utils.test.ts`, `use-session-state-cache.test.tsx`, `delta-flush.test.tsx`). ## Notes / possible follow-up The backend's `_probe_credentials` (`tui_gateway/server.py`) only checks `agent.api_key`, so OAuth providers never get a `credential_warning` on `session.info` — extending it would surface the problem even before the first send. Left out of this PR to keep it desktop-scoped.
